Supervisor (16 Sep 2026): on-ground verify, and user action is easier to demo. No driver app. No radio/GPS hardware.

---

## Recommendation

Do not free the unit at hospital. Do not split first-aid vs hospital. Do not give the driver a Free button. Keep auto-assign. If Ahmed later adds one tap for Sir Ahmed, it is dispatcher **Mark served**, and that tap must not flip `AVAILABLE`.

Hospital-free is the right *real* rule, and it is the wrong demo. The live slice already proves nearest-BUSY then next-AVAILABLE. Hospital delivery is a second trip, a second destination, and a second clock. Rehearsal still needs A-02 back in the pool after each run. If you wait for a fake hospital arrival, every rehearsal gets longer and the seed is easier to dirty.

Honest line for the script: for this demo the unit returns to the pool when the request is closed, not when a patient is handed over.

### The three ideas, unmixed

**Zain: first-aid vs hospital.** Job: when the unit may re-enter the `AVAILABLE` pool (care path). Demo: no. Phone chips Cardiac/Accident are not even sent to the API.

**Ibad: driver declares free.** Job: who attests the van is actually clear. Demo: no. You have no driver product. Supervisor also preferred a tap you can show.

**Ahmed: dispatcher marks done.** Job: who attests the crew was actually sent (Dispatch Request Served). Demo: yes, as highlight-clear only. Not as FREE.

**Sir Ahmed: two-level dispatch.** System request vs on-ground served. Matches Ahmed. Do not fold this into `AVAILABLE`.

If you add Mark served: after POST assign, the row is highlighted as a Dispatch Request. The dispatcher phones or shouts the crew, then taps Served. Queue highlight goes away. Unit stays `BUSY` until the existing complete path. Customer still sees assignment from the POST. That is the smallest thing that matches the supervisor without rewriting the slice.

---

## Jobs (stop mixing them)

People were arguing features. These are different jobs. One tap cannot do all of them.

When a request hits the board, I want the nearest free unit booked without me clicking Assign, so I can beat the clock and still show the switch. **Who: system (already built).**

When the board lights up a new job, I want to confirm a crew actually left the post, so I stop treating a software assign as a van on the road. **Who: dispatcher (Mark served).**

When the van is at my gate, I want to say they arrived, so I stop watching a timer and believe a person. **Who: customer (optional tap).**

When the patient is handed over and the bag is restocked, I want to say this van can take another job, so we do not send a unit that is still at JPMC or still wrapping gauze. **Who: crew, or dispatcher after the crew phones in. Not the customer.**

Today `COMPLETE` runs when the 15s sim hits the pickup point, then PATCH sets `AVAILABLE`. That is the customer-arrival job wearing the fleet-clear job. Hospital-free is the right fleet job. Wiring it into this demo still mixes clocks. Driver-free is the same fleet job with a product you refused to build.

Dispatcher emotional/social: not be blamed when the system assigned a unit that never moved; look in control when three jobs hit at once. Ahmed's highlight is for that. Ibad's driver button is for the crew's "don't call me, I'm still busy." Different people.

---

## States

One boolean FREE/BUSY cannot hold arrived, hospital, and served. Split the request lifecycle from the van's pool status. Only `AVAILABLE` is eligible for `POST /emergency-requests`.

**Unit (fleet):** `AVAILABLE`, `BUSY`. MVP later: `EN_ROUTE`, `ON_SCENE`, `TRANSPORTING`, `AT_HOSPITAL`, `CLEARING`, `OUT_OF_SERVICE`. `CLEARING` is restock, not `AVAILABLE` yet.

**Request (the job):** `OPEN`, `ASSIGNED` (Dispatch Request), `SERVED` (Dispatch Request Served), `ON_SCENE`, `COMPLETED`. First-aid vs hospital only changes whether `TRANSPORTING` exists. It does not invent a second app.

Who may flip `AVAILABLE`:

- POST assign (atomic AVAILABLE to BUSY): request `ASSIGNED`, unit `BUSY`. System. Keep.
- Mark served: request `SERVED`, unit still `BUSY`. Dispatcher. Supervisor level 2.
- Arrived at pickup: request `ON_SCENE`, unit still `BUSY`. Customer tap, or demo timer. Not FREE.
- Treat on scene (first-aid path, MVP): still open, still `BUSY`. Crew phones dispatcher, or future crew UI.
- At hospital / handover (MVP): still open, still `BUSY`. Same. GPS at a hospital pin is a hint, not a flip.
- Clear / complete: request `COMPLETED`, unit `AVAILABLE`. Demo: existing PATCH after the run. Real: dispatcher after crew reports clear. Never auto from map alone.

Refuse in code: `AVAILABLE` while an open request still points at that van. `COMPLETED` while the van is still `BUSY` (except crash recovery). `SERVED` without `ASSIGNED`. Customer tap setting `AVAILABLE`. Map geofence setting `AVAILABLE`.

---

## Service blueprint

Scenario: DHA Phase 5 customer requests an ambulance. No driver app. Crew is reached by phone. OSM map is evidence, not truth.

**As-is (what you ran)**

Request: phone confirm → POST to Render. Assign: customer reads switch copy; dispatcher sees Live + row; socket `queue.new`; no call to a crew. Travel: 15s timer, OSM markers, no van. Arrive/complete: PATCH complete sets `AVAILABLE`. If PATCH never fires, re-seed.

**Recommended demo add (one frontstage tap)**

Assign: row highlighted Dispatch Request; auto-book A-02. Mark served: dispatcher taps Served, highlight clears; human phones crew; software does not pretend that happened; customer does not wait on the dispatcher. Close request: same complete as today; `AVAILABLE` for next rehearsal.

Failure points: USB drop before PATCH leaves A-02 stuck `BUSY`. Dispatcher never marks served: board still true about booking, false about on-ground send. Treating OSM movement as FREE frees a van stuck in traffic or still unloading.

---

## How CAD actually works

Software recommends. People still attest. Auto-dispatch exists; it is reviewed, not worshipped.

Recommend / auto-allocate: rank nearest appropriate `AVAILABLE` unit. Human may override, or review auto-dispatch (SECAmb: review and amend).

Dispatch / served: stamp the assignment, page or message the crew. Crew or dispatcher marks en route (radio, MDT, or phone).

On scene / transporting / hospital: optional GPS breadcrumbs. Status is still a person or an MDT button. Geofence is assistive.

Available again: only `AVAILABLE` units are recommendable. Clear after handover and restock, not at scene arrival.

Sources: SECAmb Dispatch SOP; BJA CAD unit status; [SIEHS 1122, 2026](https://www.siehs.org/2026/05/from-call-to-care-what-happens-when-you-call-1122-for-an-ambulance/) (ProQA triage, CAD/GIS, data to crew tablet while caller still on the line).

**Karachi / Sindh public picture.** SIEHS 1122: central C&CC, GIS/CAD, scripted triage, GPS view of the fleet, dispatch packet to a crew tablet. That is a driver/crew device, which you are not building. 2012 ACEP survey of Edhi vs Aman: both had a control room; van-to-control was cellular phones; Edhi navigation was landmarks and vans sat at high-traffic intersections; Aman used maps, catchment stations, and trained acuity triage. Chhipa publishes emergency centres at roundabouts and near government hospitals, not a CAD whitepaper.

Copy: recommend nearest `AVAILABLE`, keep a human served/clear step, never treat map position as `AVAILABLE`. Drop: ProQA, tablets, AVL hardware. Your OSM map is closer to Aman's old Google Maps picture than to 1122's tablet loop.

---

## Karachi questions (public sources, not a field interview)

**1. Standpoint or stop anywhere?** They wait at posts, then they are wherever the last job left them until they return. That is not "stop anywhere as a doctrine." Edhi (2012): stations, vans at high-traffic accident intersections. Aman (2012): catchment stations. SIEHS: 39 stations across Sindh, GPS nearest unit rather than one central depot. Chhipa: centres at prominent places, roundabouts, near government hospitals. Madad+ seed points in DHA Phase 5 already match "post." Dynamic "clear wherever you are" is MVP and needs tracking you do not have.

**2. Do they refill supplies? How often?** International EMS SOPs: start-of-shift inventory, then restock used items after each call before the unit is really `AVAILABLE`, often at hospital or station. If critical stock is missing, the unit stays out of service or a backup is sent. I did not find a Karachi-specific published restock interval for Edhi/Chhipa/1122. Do not put a number in the thesis. Ask in the interview. In product terms, restock is the `CLEARING` state, which is why scene-arrival must not mean FREE.

**3. How does a dispatcher system work?** Call in. Location + what's wrong. Software (or a human with a map) picks a free unit. Crew is told while the caller may still be on the line. Statuses get updated as the job moves. Unit returns to the recommendable pool after clear. Multiple simultaneous jobs: the queue holds them; the dispatcher gives one crew one job by voice; CAD warns if you assign a busy unit.

Tracking without a driver app and without vehicle GPS: you are not tracking vans. You are tracking what people typed. Ibad's "how do we track multiple moving ambulances" has no honest software answer under your hardware ban. Demo: markers at seed coords or a timer. Real data later: GPS on the van (hardware) or a crew phone (the driver part you skipped).

How the dispatcher tells the crew with no driver portal: phone call from the board: unit label, address, nature. Same as the 2012 Karachi cellular pattern. The queue is how you avoid mixing two jobs onto one van. Mark served is how you record that the sentence was actually said.

---

## Interview script (Karachi dispatcher or station in-charge, ~40 min)

Goal: hear how a Karachi control room actually clears a unit, posts vans, restocks, and handles two jobs at once. Not a product pitch.

**Introduction (3 min).** Students at IBA building a small dispatcher + customer demo. We are not selling software. We will not name you without permission. You can skip any question. Recording? ask.

**Warm-up (5 min).** What is your role on a normal shift? Roughly how many calls land in an hour on a busy evening? Walk me through the last shift that felt typical, from sitting down to standing up.

**Core (20 min).**

Posts and movement. Where is the van when it is waiting for a job? After a drop-off, where does it go next? If two vans are both "free," how do you choose? Probe: "What happened last time the nearest van was not actually free?"

Passing the job with no app. When a new call is accepted, how does the crew find out? If three calls arrive together, how do you keep which crew has which address? Probe: "Tell me about a time the crew went to the wrong place."

When the van is free. At what moment do you treat that van as available for the next patient? Who tells you that? What if they arrived at the house but are still treating? What if they are at the hospital door but not done with handover? Probe: "Has the map ever shown them somewhere that did not match what they said?"

Supplies. After a call, what has to happen to the bag or the oxygen before you would send them again? Where does that happen? What if you cannot replace something?

**Scenarios (10 min).** A. Cardiac at home, treat on scene, no hospital. When is the van free? B. Accident, load and go to JPMC, two more calls waiting. What do you do with the van that is still at JPMC? C. You assigned a van in the system but the driver never moved. How do you find out?

**Wrap-up (5 min).** If a student project could only get one status from a human, which status would you want? Anything we should have asked? Thank you.

Facilitator: do not ask "would an app help?" until the end, if at all. Do not correct them with CAD vocabulary. If they say wireless or phone, write the channel. Time-box supplies if they go into inventory lists.

---

## Research park (do not let MVP rewrite the slice)

**Supervisor: user action is easier to demo.** High. Explicit. Sir Ahmed Akhtar, 16 Sep 2026: physical on-ground verifiability or map; later "user interaction is more accurate and easy to demonstrate." Validated for demo policy.

**Two-level dispatch is request vs served, not FREE.** High. Dispatch Request then Dispatch Request Served. Matches Ahmed's highlight/mark done. Must not set `AVAILABLE`.

**Karachi vans sit on posts, not a free-roam model.** Medium. Public: Edhi 2012 intersections; Aman catchment stations; SIEHS station network; Chhipa roundabouts/hospitals. Not a field interview.

**1122 sends a packet to a crew tablet; you are not building that.** High. SIEHS 2026 "From Call to Care." Conflicts with "no driver portal" and "no hardware." Demo substitute: voice/phone from dispatcher, recorded as Mark served.

**Restock frequency in Karachi is unknown.** Low. International EMS: after each call + shift check. No Edhi/Chhipa interval found. Do not design a restock timer. Needs interview.

**Scene arrival currently flips AVAILABLE in Madad+.** High. 15s timer then PATCH complete. Demo keeps it as request-closed, labeled honestly.

**Customer Cardiac/Accident chips are not a care path.** High. Flutter details are local UI. POST body is lat, lng, type ambulance. First-aid vs hospital is not in the contract.

# 1. Tracking comparison matrix

CAD means the control-room software that holds incidents and units. AVL (and cousins AVLS / AVLT) means a device in the van that reports coordinates. MDT means a screen in the cab. Last-known means the last place a person or a device reported, with a time on it. A trail is a stream of those points. OSM tiles are the map drawing, not a location sensor.

| Capability | Netherlands (LS-IV / AVLS) | US 911 CAD | India 108 (EMRI) | Karachi SIEHS 1122 | Karachi Edhi (2012 survey) | Madad+ now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Moving-van position | Supported. LS-IV collects position and status and shows vans on the control-room map (Ambulancezorg Nederland). Signal: vehicle AVLS. | Supported where AVL is installed. NENA EIDO (2021+) treats an AVL position change as an automatic incident update. Georgia equips 911 ambulances with AVLS gateways (Georgia Trauma Commission). Signal: GPS box / gateway. | Supported. EMRI lists AVLT (automatic vehicle location and tracking) plus GIS/GPRS. 2016 tender buys AVLT GPS units (EMRI). Signal: GPS box. | Supported in org copy. C&CC has GIS/CAD and a fleet-wide map view. Dispatch data goes to the crew tablet. GPS used to pick nearest unit (SIEHS, 2025-2026). Signal: GPS + tablet. Independent audit of the device: source not found. | Absent as a product. Landmark navigation. Van-to-control is cellular phone (Annals of Emergency Medicine abstract 342, 2012). Signal: phone voice. | Absent. Seed lat/lng. 15s timer. OSM on the dispatcher only. Signal: none in the van. |
| Last-known / unit status on the board | Supported. Status and position feed the meldkamer (Ambulancezorg Nederland). Signal: AVLS + CAD status. | Supported. CAD holds unit status. Crew or AVL can change it (NENA EIDO: arrived, clearing). Signal: MDT tap or AVL. | Supported. Call centre dispatches nearest available unit (EMRI). Signal: CAD + AVLT. | Partial. GPS nearest-unit plus tablet packet while the caller is still on the line (SIEHS, 2026). How “clear” is stamped: interview-still-needed. | Partial. Command centre exists. Navigation by landmark. Phone to control (2012). Signal: dispatcher + driver phone. | Partial. AVAILABLE / BUSY only. No last-known time. PATCH complete sets AVAILABLE after the timer. Signal: system timer. |
| Job packet into the vehicle | Supported. GMS → LS-IV → ambulance navigation (Ambulancezorg Nederland). Signal: in-vehicle data. | Supported where MDTs exist. CAD-to-responder is a stated EIDO path (NENA). Signal: MDT. | Partial. EMRI lists a mobile application. Field packet vs radio split: source not found, do not use in thesis. | Supported in org copy. Tablet gets the incident during the call (SIEHS, 2026). Signal: crew tablet. | Absent. Phone / landmarks (2012). Signal: voice. | Absent. No driver product. Ahmed’s board is for the room. |
| Voice path to crew (no extra device from you) | Supported. C2000 radio sits beside GMS (C2000 / AZN numbering plan). OUT OF SCOPE for Madad+ to build. | Supported. Radio remains standard even with AVL (NHTSA CAD interoperability, 2022). | Partial. Call centre plus vehicle tech. Voice vs data mix: interview-still-needed for a Karachi analogue. | Partial. Central C&CC. How Karachi crews are hailed if the tablet fails: interview-still-needed. | Supported. Cellular phones, both Edhi and Aman (2012). | Absent in software. Human in the room must phone or shout. Demo never talks to a crew. |
| Recommend nearest free unit | Supported. Fastest-available van from live position + status (AZN LS-IV page). | Supported in CAD. Still reviewed by a dispatcher (SECAmb auto-dispatch is the UK cousin: nearest resource on CAD, humans amend). | Supported. Nearest available 108 unit (EMRI). | Supported in org copy. GPS nearest (SIEHS). | Partial. Human picks using landmarks / stations (2012). Aman had acuity triage. Edhi did not. | Supported. POST auto-assign. A-05 BUSY → A-02. |
| Human “we actually sent them” | Supported. Centralist still tasks the unit on GMS. AVLS does not replace the send. | Supported. Dispatch is a person or a rule the person can override (NHTSA, 2022; SECAmb Dispatch SOP, 2024). | Partial. Dispatch officer in the loop (EMRI). Served-stamp UX: source not found. | Partial. Dispatch starts during the call (SIEHS, 2026). On-ground “left the bay” stamp: interview-still-needed. | Supported by voice. Phone call is the send. | Absent. Queue row appears. No Mark served. Sir Ahmed (16 Sep 2026) asked for Dispatch Request Served. |
| AVAILABLE after clear, not at the house | Supported as CAD practice. Status returns to the pool after the job (AZN: status + position). Exact restock rule: source not found. | Supported. EIDO lists clearing as its own operation (NENA). | Partial. Unit must be available to be assigned (EMRI). Restock interval: source not found, do not use in thesis. | Unclear. Org copy covers dispatch and hospital handover. When the van re-enters the pool: interview-still-needed. Karachi restock frequency: source not found, do not use in thesis. | Unclear. Phone-in is the plausible channel (2012). | Demo shortcut. Timer hits pickup → PATCH → AVAILABLE. That is not handover. |

**Source tags (research-repository)**

| Bucket | Layer | Item | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| international CAD | Study / agency spec | Ambulancezorg Nederland LS-IV; Nationaal Nummerplan (AVLS, GMS, C2000); SECAmb Dispatch SOP (2024); NHTSA CAD interoperability (2022); NENA EIDO FAQ; Georgia AVLS program; EMRI technology page + 2016 AVLT tender | Medium-high for “a device reports position.” Low for copying their UX. |
| Karachi public | Study | ACEP abstract 342 (2012): Edhi landmarks + phones; Aman Google Maps + phones; Chhipa did not sit the interview | Medium, dated. |
| Karachi public | Raw / org | SIEHS 2025-2026 web: GIS/CAD, tablet packet, GPS nearest, 39 stations | Low-medium. Self-description. |
| Karachi public | Raw | 2013 visitor note of Aman wall map with moving flags (Sarwar / journalist) | Low. Observation, not a methods paper. |
| Madad+ demo | Insight | Phone POST + dispatcher queue work against Render. OSM replaced Google Maps. No device in a van. | High for the slice you ran. |
| interview-still-needed |, | Who says “clear” in a Karachi room. What happens if the 1122 tablet is dead. Restock. Edhi 2026 vs 2012. |, |

**Reality-checker:** Madad+ as a tracker of vans: **NEEDS WORK**. Seed pins, a 15s timer, and OSM tiles are a drawing. Verdict stays NEEDS WORK until a human stamp or a device exists.

**GIS (last-known vs trail):** Last-known is one WGS84 point plus a clock. A trail is many points from a sensor. OSM is the basemap. Drawing a line between post and pickup is interpolation. It is not AVL.

# 2. Jobs (do not mix)

1. When a request hits the board, I want the nearest free unit booked without me clicking Assign, so the switch still fires on the clock. **Who: system (already built). Emotional: beat the clock. Social: look in control.** This is dispatch, not tracking.

2. When the row lights up, I want to confirm a crew left the post, so a software assign is not treated as a van on the road. **Who: dispatcher. Mark served. Emotional: not blamed for a van that never moved.**

3. When several vans are out, I want a last-known place with a time, so I can talk to the right crew and I do not invent a trail. **Who: dispatcher, after the phone they already have. Tracking is this job only.**

4. When the patient is handed over and the bag is usable again, I want this van in the AVAILABLE pool, so the next POST does not send a unit still at JPMC or still wrapping gauze. **Who: dispatcher after the crew phones in. Never the customer. Never the map.**

# 3. Service blueprint (as-is vs software-only)

Scenario: DHA Phase 5 customer requests an ambulance. No driver app. Crew reached by phone. OSM is evidence. Hardware you will not build (AVL box, crew tablet, C2000, 108 AVLT) sits in Support and is **OUT OF SCOPE**.

**As-is (what you ran)**

| Lane | Request | Assign | Travel | Arrive / close |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Evidence | Confirm screen | Switch copy A-05 busy, A-02 assigned. Dispatcher Live + row | OSM markers at seed. Phone 15s screens | Request complete. A-02 AVAILABLE on GET /ambulances |
| Customer | Tap REQUEST NOW | Reads A-02 | Watches timer | Sees complete |
| Frontstage |, | Queue row, marker BUSY | Markers sit or fake-walk | Marker AVAILABLE |
| Backstage | POST to Render | Auto AVAILABLE→BUSY. Socket queue.new | No call to a crew | PATCH complete |
| Support | Render, seed | Sockets, OSM | OSM tiles. AVL/tablet OUT OF SCOPE | Same |
| Fail | Cold start 45s | USB drop. Seed dirty if A-02 already BUSY | Treating OSM as a van | PATCH never fires. Re-seed |

**Recommended software-only (after this demo; demo slice unchanged until then)**

| Lane | Request | Assign | Mark served | Scene | Close |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Evidence | Same POST | Highlight: Dispatch Request. Auto-book A-02 | Highlight off. Last-known = left post, time stamped | Pin jumps to pickup. Last-known = at pickup | Pin stays. AVAILABLE only here |
| Customer | REQUEST NOW | Sees assignment from POST. Does not wait on served | Optional: “crew at my gate” | Same | Complete as today for rehearsal |
| Frontstage |, | Ahmed: highlighted row | Dispatcher tap Served | Dispatcher or customer: at pickup | Dispatcher or existing PATCH for demo rehearsal |
| Backstage | POST | Ibad: request ASSIGNED, unit BUSY | ASSIGNED→SERVED. Unit still BUSY. Phone the crew | ON_SCENE. Still BUSY | COMPLETED. AVAILABLE |
| Support | Render | Sockets | Phone they already own. No new radio | OSM jump, no trail | Same |
| Fail | Same | Same | Never tapped: board true about booking, false about send | Customer tap must not PATCH | USB drop still dirties seed |

# 4. States and forbidden flips

Two machines. Only AVAILABLE units may be chosen by `POST /emergency-requests`.

**Unit:** AVAILABLE, BUSY. Later optional (do not build for this demo): EN_ROUTE, ON_SCENE, TRANSPORTING, CLEARING, OUT_OF_SERVICE. CLEARING is restock, still not AVAILABLE.

**Request:** OPEN, ASSIGNED (Dispatch Request), SERVED (Dispatch Request Served), ON_SCENE, COMPLETED.

| # | Event | Allowed result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | POST assign | Unit AVAILABLE→BUSY. Request OPEN→ASSIGNED |
| 2 | Mark served (dispatcher) | Request ASSIGNED→SERVED. Unit stays BUSY |
| 3 | At pickup (dispatcher after phone, or customer “at my gate”) | Request → ON_SCENE. Unit stays BUSY |
| 4 | Clear / complete (dispatcher after crew reports, or current PATCH for the live demo only) | Request COMPLETED. Unit BUSY→AVAILABLE |

| # | Forbidden | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Map / geofence / OSM pin sets AVAILABLE | GPS will lie in traffic, under a flyover, or in a glove box. Sir asked for a tap (16 Sep 2026). |
| 6 | Customer tap sets AVAILABLE | Patient does not put a city van back in the pool. |
| 7 | Mark served sets AVAILABLE | Served means sent, not free. |
| 8 | ON_SCENE sets AVAILABLE in the FYP build | House arrival is not handover. Demo A still PATCHes at the timer. Name that lie in the script until B ships. |
| 9 | AVAILABLE while an open request still points at that van | Double-book. |
| 10 | SERVED without ASSIGNED | Cannot attest a send that was never booked. |
| 11 | Interpolated OSM path stored as position | Trail without a device. |
| 12 | Customer Mark served | Customer cannot see the bay. |

# 5. Concept selection (winner + cost)

**Criteria frozen before the three options**

Thresholds (fail = out): no new hardware; no driver portal; demo auto-assign stays; AVAILABLE is not set by the map.

Trade-offs: honesty of location; extra dispatcher taps per job; rehearsal minutes; thesis credibility.

**Three concepts**

**A. Incumbent (seed pin + 15s timer + PATCH).** Passes every threshold. Extra taps: 0. Rehearsal stays short. Honesty of location: fail if you call it tracking. Thesis: fail if the script says the map follows vans. Keep this for the **current demo**.

**B. Status-derived last-known.** Auto-assign stays. Dispatcher Mark served (1 tap). Pin jumps on status: post → pickup on ON_SCENE. No trail. AVAILABLE only on complete/clear. Extra taps: 1 required (served), 1 optional (at pickup) if the customer does not stamp the gate. Rehearsal: add a few seconds if you show served. Honesty: last-known with a clock, which is what you can defend. Thesis: matches SECAmb/NENA “human still attests” without copying Georgia/108 hardware.

**C. Interpolated moving OSM marker.** No device. Pin slides post→pickup on a timer. Extra taps: 0. Looks like Netherlands/US/108 AVL. Honesty: fail. Thesis: fail. If anyone then auto-frees on the pin, it also fails threshold 4.

**Rejected before ranking:** GPS boxes, OBD, crew tablets. Fail threshold 1. Do not spec Ibad installing them. 108 AVLT and Georgia AVLS are the reason those countries have a moving map. You chose not to buy that.

**Winner for the remaining FYP months: B.** Owner: you (product), Ahmed (served + pin jump), Ibad (`served` + last-known fields), Zain (optional at-gate, never FREE).

**What B costs.** You give up a moving trail. Dispatcher absorbs 1 tap per job (Tesler: that tap is inherent once hardware is banned). Rehearsal is a bit longer if you insist on showing served. Customer may absorb at-gate because only they can see the driveway.

**What A costs if you never leave it.** The exhibition still works. The tracking chapter has to say the demo does not track vans.

**What would bring C back.** A device in the van. Not a prettier Leaflet animation.

**Who should update last-known (recommendation you asked for).** Dispatcher, after the phone they already have. That is the 2012 Karachi pattern (cellular van-to-control) without pretending you are 1122’s tablet loop. Offer the customer only “crew at my gate.” That is ON_SCENE. It never sets AVAILABLE.

**Hassle count (Tesler, not a vibe)**

| Horizon | Extra dispatcher taps per job | Who absorbs tracking |
|---|---|---|
| This demo | 0 | Product (timer). Script must say so. |
| FYP B | 1 (served). 2 if customer never stamps the gate | Dispatcher for send and last-known. Customer optional for the driveway. Map never. |

# 6. Karachi interview questions still needed

Participant: dispatcher or station in-charge. About 40 minutes. Goal: last-known and clear. Do not pitch the app. Facilitator: skip “would an app help?”

1. Walk me through the last shift that felt typical, from sitting down to standing up.

2. When a van is waiting for a job, where is it, and who knows that?

3. After you accept a call, how does that crew find out where to go? What happened last time that message did not land?

4. If two jobs arrive together, how do you keep which crew has which address?

5. At what moment do you treat that van as free for the next patient? Who tells you? Probe: arrived at the house but still treating. Probe: at the hospital door, handover not done.

6. Has a map or a phone location ever shown a van somewhere that did not match what the crew said? What did you trust?

7. After a call, what has to happen to the bag or the oxygen before you would send them again? Where does that happen? (No number unless they volunteer one.)

8. If you could get only one status from a human on a busy night, which status would you want, and what goes wrong when you do not get it?

# 7. What to say in the demo script (max 12 bullets)

- We auto-assign the nearest free unit. That is why A-05 is skipped and A-02 goes.
- The dispatcher map is OSM. It shows last booked or seed position.
- There is no box in the van and no driver phone app in this build.
- A moving pin in 1122, 108, Georgia, or Dutch LS-IV comes from a device or a tablet. We did not build that.
- For this demo the unit returns to the pool when the request is closed on the timer, not when a patient is handed over.
- If the teacher asks who is free: BUSY means assigned. AVAILABLE means the complete call ran.
- If Ahmed has Mark served by then: this tap means a human sent the crew. It does not free the van.
- If the customer taps at-gate by then: that means they see the crew. It does not free the van.
- Karachi restock timing: we do not have a published number, so we do not quote one.
- Abandoned run: check GET /ambulances. If A-02 is stuck BUSY, re-seed before the next pass.
- Wake Render on /health before anyone taps REQUEST NOW.
- Tracking claim for Madad+: NEEDS WORK. The slice you are showing is assign + switch + complete.

**WORKFLOW: status-derived last-known (winner B only)**  
**Version:** 0.1 **Date:** 2026-09-17 **Status:** Draft **Trigger:** customer REQUEST NOW while dispatcher is on Render.

Prerequisites: Render /health ok. Seed A-05 BUSY, A-02 AVAILABLE. Phone on current build. Ahmed BACKEND_URL = Render. OSM inits. No AVL.

Happy path: POST ASSIGNED A-02 → row highlighted → dispatcher phones crew → Mark served (BUSY stays) → last-known “left post” + time → optional ON_SCENE (pin jumps to pickup) → complete/clear → AVAILABLE. Zain does not wait on served to see assignment.

Handoffs: Zain POST/PATCH ↔ Ibad Render ↔ Ahmed `dispatch` room. Served payload: `{requestId, status: SERVED, assignedAmbulance, lastKnown: {lat, lng, label, at}}`. Timeout 45s on POST. On timeout: user retry, no auto-retry.

Failures: cold start → wake /health. USB drop before PATCH → re-seed. Served never tapped → booking still true, send false, pin stays at post. OSM blank → queue still counts. Two REQUEST NOW → stop, re-seed. Interpolated trail or geofence FREE → refuse in Ibad’s API.

Observable: customer sees assignment then optional at-gate. Dispatcher sees highlight then last-known time. DB: request status, unit BUSY/AVAILABLE, lastKnownAt. Logs: POST, served, complete.

Cleanup: leftover BUSY from a dead USB session is Ibad re-seed. No AVL resource to destroy.

Assumptions: the station already has a phone. Last-known labels are post / pickup only until someone interviews a hospital clear. Chhipa 2026 tracking: source not found.

</answer>

The user asked:

ill be very honest i didnt understand a word of what you said. use @.cursor/rules/humanizer.md to summarise each sections findings.

The reply recorded:

**1. Other countries vs Karachi vs us**

Places like the Netherlands, parts of the US, and India's 108 service can watch a van crawl across a control-room map because a box or a tablet in the vehicle keeps sending coordinates back to the people booking jobs. Edhi, in a 2012 study, ran on landmarks and a phone call into the control room. Sindh's 1122 website describes the GPS-and-tablet setup. Our app books A-02 and paints OSM pins where the seed file put them. Those pins sit on planted coordinates.

**2. Four jobs**

The WhatsApp thread mashed four jobs into one argument. Job one is the computer picking the nearest free van, which you already do. Job two is a person confirming the crew actually left the post. Job three is somebody reporting the last place they heard that van was. Job four is putting the van back in the pool for the next patient. Tracking is job three.

**3. How the service runs today, and later**

Right now the customer taps request, Ahmed's board gets a row, fifteen seconds tick, complete frees A-02. Nobody phones a driver. After this demo, keep that booking. Add a dispatcher tap that means "I told the crew." Then jump the pin to the house when a person says they got there.

**4. What each status means**

Assigned means the computer gave that van the job. Served means a human sent them. At the house means someone saw them at the gate. Free means the job is closed and the van can be booked again. Only complete (or a later "clear" tap) puts the van back in the pool. The map does not. The patient does not. The "I sent them" tap leaves the van busy.

**5. What to actually do**

Keep the exhibition run as it is, timer and all. After that, build the human-report version: one extra tap for "sent," then a pin jump for last place heard. Skip a cartoon van sliding across OSM. Skip buying GPS boxes. The cost is one extra dispatcher tap per job, two if the customer never says the crew arrived.

**6. What you still have to ask a real dispatcher**

Web pages do not say who in a Karachi room declares a van free, or how often bags get restocked. Sit with a dispatcher or station in-charge and ask where vans wait, how the crew hears the address, and at what moment they treat a van as free. Leave restock numbers out of the thesis until that person answers.

**7. What you say out loud in the demo**

The trick on screen is auto-assign: A-05 was closer, A-02 got it. The map is OSM over planted positions. The van goes free when the request is closed on the timer. If someone brings up 1122's moving fleet, that setup uses a gadget in the van, which this project left out.

The user asked:

so how do we as students implement ambulance tracking? you didnt answer that

The reply recorded:

Fair, I buried the actual answer under research. Here's the build, plainly.

**You cannot show a van moving live.** No box in the vehicle, no driver phone, nothing to poll for coordinates. Any "moving pin" you fake is a lie, and I already told you not to sell that to your supervisor.

**What you can build instead:** a status board that jumps a pin between fixed points, updated by a human tap. That is a real, honest thing to build, and it is your tracking feature.

**Concretely, on your stack:**

1. **Backend (Ibad):** add one field to the request, `lastKnownStatus`, with values `AT_BASE`, `LEFT_BASE`, `AT_PICKUP`, `AT_HOSPITAL`, `CLEAR`. Add a `PATCH /emergency-requests/:id/status` endpoint that only a dispatcher action can call. Each time it's called, stamp `lastKnownAt = now()` and emit it over the existing `dispatch` socket room the same way `ambulance.updated` already works.

2. **Web dispatcher (Ahmed):** on each queue row, add small buttons: "Mark served" (sets `LEFT_BASE`) and "At pickup" (sets `AT_PICKUP`). Tapping one calls that PATCH. When the socket event comes back, move the OSM marker to whichever fixed coordinate matches that status (base coords, pickup coords you already have from the request, hospital coords if you add one). No animation, no interpolation, it jumps, because that's honest about what you know.

3. **Mobile (you):** nothing new required. Optionally show "crew has left the station" / "crew reported at pickup" text on the customer screen, sourced from the same socket event, so the phone side reflects the same taps.

4. **What stays exactly as-is:** `POST /emergency-requests` still auto-assigns nearest AVAILABLE unit. `PATCH .../complete` still flips the unit back to AVAILABLE, that part of your state machine doesn't change. The new status field never touches AVAILABLE/BUSY. It only changes what the pin shows and what the dispatcher log says.

**Why this counts as "implementing tracking" for a thesis:** you're not claiming GPS. You're claiming a dispatcher-attested location log, which is literally what Edhi ran on with a phone in 2012, just captured in a database instead of nobody's memory. That's a legitimate, buildable, defensible feature for a demo and for the write-up.

**Effort:** this is a half-day for Ibad (one field, one endpoint, one socket emit) and a half-day for Ahmed (two buttons, marker-jump logic he likely already has since markers already move on `ambulance.updated`). Nothing here touches your locked demo slice, build and test it as an addition, don't rip out the current 15-second flow.

If you want, I can write this as an exact `@.cursor/rules/workflow-architect.mdc`-style spec (endpoint payload, socket event shape, button-to-status mapping) that Ibad and Ahmed can implement straight off of.

The user asked:

this chat is a continuation of madad+ v3, madad+ v3 demo sprint, madad+ v3.1(making sure all 3 stuff work togeth..., madad+ v3.2, madad+ queries and all other linked chats. our demo was held on saturday, 4 days back. our teacher liked what we did, but ibad had accidentally set all ambulances to busy so we couldn't show him the part on the app where the ambulance is dispatched and arrives at the users home. after that, we did some more brainstorming. ibad fixed the issue too.

for emergency services:
we decided on making a driver portal so that, when a user calls the ambulance, the dispatcher portal(by the way, we decided to automate the dispatcher portal) looks at the nearest available ambulance and automatically dispatches it. there is a manual override option, but ill talk about that in a bit
for the dispatcher portal, like i said, we decided to automate about 98%? of it, with a manual override option available for the dispatcher. in the dispatch system, we decided to change the states of ambulances so that ambulances are either FREE, BUSY or UNAVAILABLE. the first two are straightforward. for the UNAVAILABLE state, there are two cases:
1. if an ambulance, on the way, gets a tire burst, or engine issue, or doesnt have enough petrol to make it, the driver can make itself UNAVAILABLE and the dispatcher system then assigns the next available driver nearest to the users location
2. if an ambulance picks up the user and on the way to the hospital gets into an issue, like a tire burst, engine issue etc, the driver can make himself UNAVAILABLE, and the app will then ping his location to the driver nearest to the ambulance's current location who can then, in a way, "transfer" the patient.

for all cases, including the two above, the dispatcher portal(website that ahmed made) will have 3 tabs: free, busy and unavailable. all three are pretty self explanatory. the dispatcher will also and always have an option to override the decision of the system and choose if an ambulance can go to a user or if another one is allowed to.

domestic services:
for the domestic services, we settled on: carpenter, plumber and electrician. the process will be very similar to what the Karsaz app does: user asks for a service, explains his needs, the request goes to all nearby relevant domestic providers, and one will accept it.
the financial model is what ahmed came up with:
to start off, the basic service/inspection fee will be fixed. there are 2 cases:
1. a service provider can show up to a users house and inspect an issue, say, a broken AC. he could then list down what parts need changing/repairing and then list them in the app alongside their price. if the user is happy with the price or successfully negotiates it a bit lower, the user can then mark the charges as acceptable, and the user will be charged for the parts + the inspection fee, which is fixed.
2. if in the event the user is not in agreement of the price and cannot successfully renegotiate a lower price, the provider will just charge the fixed inspection fee.

in all cases, the fixed inspection charges will be based on a radius. so if a provider is within, for example, 5km of a users location, he will be charged x rupees, and for every, say, 1km farther away any provider is that is free, the inspection charges will be x + y rupees.

Before that pickup button has been pressed, the next FREE unit is pointed at the caller's house and told to go there. Nearer unit becomes FREE while the far one is still driving, the dispatcher pulls the far one off the call, the near one takes it, and the far driver stands down and goes back to waiting. Before anyone presses pickup, the patient is still waiting at home, so the next free ambulance gets sent straight to the house. The caller's phone drops the first ambulance and shows the new one, plus a short line that the first had a problem. Patient is already aboard. The next free ambulance goes to that broken ambulance's spot on the map. The caller watches the second one drive toward the first. Once the patient is moved across, the phone says the patient is now in the second ambulance, and that ambulance continues to the hospital. Marking it FREE is a separate button. The driver does it when the ambulance can work again, and a dispatcher can do it too.

The user asked:

okay that works as intended. now we need to work on the domestic services part. list down all the updates about domestic service from the meeting

The reply recorded:

These are the domestic-service decisions from the Saturday demo follow-up, through 22 September.

- The trades are carpenter, plumber, and electrician. The AC technician and the mechanic on the v2 wireframe are swapped out for now.
- The flow follows the Karsaz pattern. The user asks for a service, explains the need, and the request goes to every nearby provider in that trade. The first one to accept takes the job. Everyone else sees it disappear.
- Jobs only go to providers inside a maximum radius. Anyone past that radius never sees the request. That radius is still unset.
- A provider who is already on a job can still accept another one. That extra job sits in a pending list. The caller is told their provider is busy and can cancel and ask someone else. If they send the same request out again, the provider they just cancelled cannot take it. Other new jobs can still land in that pending list.
- Providers receive and accept jobs in the same phone app, through a provider login.
- The inspection fee is fixed and depends on how far the accepting provider is from the house, measured at the moment they accept. Inside 5 km the fee is x. Each extra kilometre adds another y, so 7 km is x + 2y. The rupee amounts for x and y are still blank.
- After the inspection, the provider types the parts and a repair total into the app. That total does not include the inspection fee. The two sides settle a lower number in person, the provider enters the new total, and the user taps accept.
- If the user accepts, the amount owed is the inspection fee plus the agreed repair total. If they refuse, only the inspection fee is owed. The app records what is owed. Whether the user pays inside the app or outside it is still open.

The user asked:

now list down everything that the domestic service portion of our project will contain, including the post demo updates

The reply recorded:

The domestic side is the customer booking path, the provider job path, and the money rules from the Saturday follow-up. The follow-up replaces the old category list and the old price screen.

**Customer**
- A Services entry from home, plus a Services tab.
- Three trades: carpenter, plumber, and electrician. The AC technician, mechanic, and painter on the wireframe come out.
- A trade screen with the kinds of jobs that trade does, an issue choice, and a book button.
- A description: a specific issue, a written note, and a photo.
- A location: a saved home, a saved office, a point on the map, and a landmark.
- A time: as soon as possible, or a later date and time.
- A confirm screen, then a search screen the user can cancel.
- The request goes to every matching provider inside a maximum radius. Anyone past that radius never sees it. That radius is still unset.
- The first provider to accept takes the job. Every other provider sees it disappear.
- If that provider is already on another job, the user is told they are busy and can cancel and ask someone else. The provider who was just cancelled cannot take that same request again.
- Once someone accepts, the user sees the provider's name, rating, review count, distance, and ETA, and can track them on a map, call, chat, or open their profile.
- An en-route screen, then a screen for work in progress, with a way to contact support.
- A final-cost review the user can accept or report as a problem.
- A finished screen with a star rating and an optional written review, which the user can skip.
- A Requests tab with an active job and a history. A completed plumber job is the domestic example already in the wireframe.
- A loading state and an error state for the services list.

**Money**
- The inspection fee is fixed from the accepting provider's distance to the house, measured when they accept. Inside 5 km it is x. Each extra kilometre adds y, so 7 km is x + 2y. The rupee amounts are still blank.
- After the visit, the provider enters the parts and a repair total. That total does not include the inspection fee.
- The two sides can settle a lower repair number in person. The provider types the new total, and the user accepts it, negotiates, or refuses.
- Accepting means the amount owed is the inspection fee plus the agreed repair total. Refusing means only the inspection fee is owed.
- The app records what is owed. Paying inside the app or outside it is still open, so the wireframe's cash and JazzCash choices are not settled.

**Provider**
- The same phone app, through a provider login. The wireframe reaches this from Profile as provider mode.
- A dashboard with the provider's name, trade, and rating, plus an available or offline switch.
- Incoming requests with the problem, the customer, the location, and the cost range, and buttons to accept or decline.
- A pending list for jobs accepted while the provider is already out on another job.
- After an accept: the customer is notified, the provider gets an arrival time, can navigate, and can call.
- On the job: navigate, mark the work as started, write notes, and upload photos.
- At the end: submit the parts and the repair total, plus a note on the work done.

The user asked:

and if i were to implement all this into the application, which agents and/or skills would be a perfect fit, and why?

The reply recorded:

Use these for the Flutter app. The wireframe is already the spec, so these agents build it rather than redesign it.

- **mobile-app-builder** writes the customer booking screens and the provider job screens in `madad_plus_mobile`.
- **state-machine** keeps the job in one explicit sequence: searching, accepted, en route, in progress, cost review, then finished or refused. It also keeps a busy provider’s extra accepts in a pending list, and makes the first accept close the job for everyone else.
- **navigation-patterns** separates the user tabs from provider mode. Services, the booking steps, and Requests stay on the user side. Provider mode is the only door into the provider dashboard.
- **ui-designer** matches the wireframe cards, issue chips, map, and cost review, and drops the AC technician, mechanic, and painter.
- **form-design** covers the problem description, photo, location, schedule, and the provider’s parts list and repair total.
- **loading-states** and **error-handling-ux** cover the services loading and error screens, cancel during search, and Report an issue on the cost review.
- **minimal-change-engineer** leaves the emergency and driver flows alone, and leaves admin, the dispatcher site, and in-app payment out. Paying inside the app or outside it is still undecided.

Add **backend-architect** and **realtime-collaboration-engineer** only when one phone has to tell the others that a provider accepted, that a job moved to pending, or that a cancelled provider cannot take that same request again. **payments-billing-engineer** waits until you decide whether the recorded debt is collected in the app.

## State model
Model one domestic job as explicit states. Use the @.cursor/skills/state-machine/SKILL.md skill.

Customer job, one value at a time:
- idle
- searching
- assigned
- enRoute
- inProgress
- costReview
- refused
- complete

Provider duty, one value at a time:
- offline
- available
- onJob

A second accepted job while duty is onJob is pending. Pending is a list of at most one demo job, not a second active job.

Opening provider mode from registration, from Sign in as provider, or from Switch to provider mode starts at available, with no active job and an empty pending list.

## Post-demo rules that replace the wireframe
These override the wireframe wherever they disagree.

Trades are carpenter, plumber, and electrician. Do not show AC technician, mechanic, or painter.

A request is offered to matching providers inside a maximum radius. The maximum radius number is not set. Until it is set, the demo provider is inside it and can see the request. Do not invent a kilometre cap.

The first accept takes the job. On this one phone, after accept, show the line "Other providers no longer see this request."

A provider who is already on a job may accept one more request. That request goes to Pending, not to the active job. The customer for that second request sees "This provider is busy" and a Cancel button. Cancel returns that customer to the services grid. Ali Khan cannot accept that same cancelled request again. He can still receive a different new request into Pending.

Inspection fee:
- distance is John Stewart's 3.2 km, measured at accept
- inside 5 km the fee is x
- each extra kilometre adds y
- 7 km would be x + 2y
- x and y have no rupee values

After the visit, the provider enters a repair total. That number does not include the inspection fee. The people settle a lower number in person. The provider types the new total. The customer can accept it or refuse it.

Accept: the amount owed is the inspection fee plus the typed repair total. Show "Amount owed: x + [typed total]".
Refuse: the amount owed is the inspection fee only. Show "Amount owed: x".
Store that string on the job. Do not open a payment screen. Do not show Cash, JazzCash, or Other.

The user asked:

for our application, list down 5 fonts which would look good for our application both visually and psychologically. dont restrict urself to just fonts on google

The reply recorded:

These five fit Madad+ because the emergency side has to stay calm and readable under stress, and the domestic side has to feel human. All of them stay clear at the small size of your tab labels and buttons.

1. **Atkinson Hyperlegible** (Braille Institute). The letters are drawn so similar shapes stay apart: a phone number, an address, and an ambulance code are harder to misread in a hurry. It feels careful rather than stylish. The family is Regular and Bold, so headlines would use Bold instead of the extra-heavy weight in the app now.

2. **Söhne** (Klim Type Foundry). Even, quiet, and slightly narrow, so a card title and a status pill sit on one line without looking cramped. Psychologically it reads as a staffed service: competent and calm, which is what you want when someone is calling an ambulance.

3. **IBM Plex Sans** (IBM). Built for interfaces, with figures that line up. That suits ETAs, distances, and the inspection fee. It feels systematic, like a dispatch tool, without turning the plumber flow into a hospital form.

4. **Saans** (Displaay). A plain sans with a little warmth in the curves. One family can cover both halves: Semibold on the red emergency card, Regular on the green service card. It feels like a person is on the way, which fits a provider coming to the house.

5. **GT America** (Grilli Type). Straightforward and a bit sturdy, with a real Black weight for “How can we help?” and “REQUEST NOW.” It feels civic and plain-spoken: public help, not a startup landing page.

Söhne or GT America is the strongest single choice if the app should feel finished. Atkinson Hyperlegible is the strongest if the priority is reading an address correctly on a bright phone screen.

for our application, list down 5 free fonts which would look good for our application both visually and psychologically. dont restrict urself to just fonts on google

The reply recorded:

The app is currently on Flutter’s default type, set against a navy, red, and green palette. These five are free for a commercial app, and each one is readable on a phone when someone is in a hurry.

1. **Atkinson Hyperlegible**, [brailleinstitute.org/freefont](https://www.brailleinstitute.org/freefont). It was drawn so that similar letters and numbers stay distinct, which matters for an address, an ETA, or a phone number. It feels plain and steady, which lowers the chance of a misread during an emergency.

2. **IBM Plex Sans**, [ibm.com/plex](https://www.ibm.com/plex). It has the tone of a public service rather than a startup. The navy and the emergency red stay serious, and the figures stay clear for distances and fees.

3. **Source Sans 3**, [github.com/adobe-fonts/source-sans](https://github.com/adobe-fonts/source-sans). Adobe built it for interface text at small sizes, so the tab labels and card subtitles stay readable. It is neutral enough that the red emergency card and the green services card still feel like one app.

4. **Public Sans**, [designsystem.digital.gov/documentation/typography](https://designsystem.digital.gov/documentation/typography/). It was made for government sites. The psychology is “this is a civic tool,” which fits a help app better than a fashion typeface.

5. **General Sans**, [fontshare.com/fonts/general-sans](https://www.fontshare.com/fonts/general-sans). It is a bit warmer than the four above, which suits booking a plumber without making the ambulance path feel casual. The Indian Type Foundry releases it free for commercial use.

Use one family for the whole app. Mixing a soft face on Services with a harsh face on Emergency makes the product feel like two apps.

## What "at the same time" means in this code

The only shared path is: the phone creates a request, the server assigns a free ambulance, and the dispatcher hears `queue.new` plus `ambulance.updated` on the `dispatch` room.

These dispatcher controls do not talk to the phone or the server. They only change the browser: map click to simulate a call, Reassign, Bar this unit, Mark free, and every button labeled Simulate. A pass on those is not a pass on the joint system.

## Setup

The user asked:

is it true that if, on the mobile branch, i do git checkout "new branch name", that new branch is a branch of mobile, or is it a branch of main? and is that how version control works?

The reply recorded:

A new branch starts from the commit you are on when you create it. On `mobile`, that commit is `e8086cb` ("new changes"), so the new branch begins there, with `mobile`'s history behind it. `main` is not involved.

Creating it looks like this:

```powershell
git checkout -b new-branch-name
```

The `-b` is what creates the branch. `git checkout new-branch-name` without `-b` only switches to a branch that already exists.

A branch is a label on a commit. It keeps that starting point, and new commits on it move only that label.

The user asked:

and so if i need to test something on, say, Web, i switch to Web on the latest commit, then use git checkout -b WebTest, then do my work, and if its good enough I merge it with Test? and if not i can discard WebTest and stay on Web's latest work?

The reply recorded:

Yes. Check out `Web` first, then create the test branch from that commit:

```powershell
git checkout Web
git checkout -b WebTest
```

`WebTest` starts at `Web`'s latest commit. Your work stays on `WebTest`.

If that work is good, check out `Web` and merge `WebTest` into it. `Web` then includes the test commits. The merge target is `Web`, the branch you started from.

If it is not good, check out `Web` and delete `WebTest`:

```powershell
git checkout Web
git branch -D WebTest
```

`Web` stays on the commit it had before the test.

The driver is the emergency driver, the person with the ambulance. The provider is the domestic service provider, a different person. Those are two roles.

That splits the demo notes. "Simulate: picked up", "Simulate: driver unavailable", and "Bar this unit" are driver controls sitting on the dispatcher. "Provider arrived" is a domestic-provider control sitting on the user's phone. The map complaint, circles driving into each other, is the ambulance map, and he wants a hospital to look different from an ambulance. On the user's map, the person coming can be either the ambulance or the domestic provider, and the screen also has to show the distance and the user's own location.

One emulator and one phone can cover the user plus one responder in a single pass. A pass for the ambulance uses the phone as the user and the emulator as the driver. A pass for the domestic service uses the phone as the user and the emulator as the provider. His request for two phones is the same shape, with a physical phone in place of the emulator. One mobile app with three sign-ins, and a dispatcher who can assign, reassign, and take a unit out of service. That matches how the phone is already built: user, driver, and provider are sign-in paths in the same app, and the website is the board.

**Hospitals**

A few fixed Karachi hospitals, always on the map, with a different icon from the ambulance dots, makes the idle board readable. Right now every mark is an ambulance, so a hospital and a unit look the same. A short list (Indus is already named on the driver screen) is enough for a demo. The gap is the trip itself: A-03 turned busy and drove until it sat on another unit, because that click never had a hospital as its destination.

Only the hospital for the current trip, drawn once a driver is heading there, explains that drive. The unit would leave toward a hospital mark instead of another ambulance. On an idle board, before any trip, the map would still be ambulance dots only, which is the screen he was looking at when he clicked A-03.

Fixed hospitals always visible, with the active trip’s hospital highlighted, covers both moments. The idle map shows where hospitals are. During a run, one of those places is the destination, and the ambulance moves toward that icon. I would keep the list short, and use the same places the driver can already be sent to.

**What to do first**

Mobile first, on `mobiletest`, is the change he led with. “Provider accepts” sits on the customer’s “Finding a provider” screen and only flips local state. The provider name on the next screen is fixed copy. Until that button lives only on the provider sign-in, a second phone has nothing real to do. The same split applies to the driver: picked up, unavailable, and reached the hospital already exist on the driver screens. Those have to be the actions that move a job. The risk is size. Domestic requests are not on the server yet, so taking the button off the user screen leaves that user waiting until the provider phone can accept the same request.

Dispatcher first, on `webtest`, is the smaller visible fix. Plain wording, a different hospital icon, and stopping a map click from turning a free unit busy are all on that site. “Bar this unit” becomes a plain out-of-service action, which is the control you want the dispatcher to keep. The risk is the simulate buttons. “Simulate: picked up” and “Simulate: driver unavailable” are the only way a demo job moves today. Removing them before the driver phone sends those updates leaves a job stuck on the board.

Both at once fits the two branches, and it fits a split where one person takes `mobiletest` and another takes `webtest`. The seam is the part that breaks: the driver marks picked up, the board must show it; the dispatcher takes a unit out of service, the driver phone must see it; the user requests a plumber, the provider phone must accept it. Two visual cleanups that do not share that path will each look fine alone and fail the two-phone test.

I would start on `mobiletest` and move the driver and provider actions off the user screens. On `webtest`, in the same stretch, change the wording, draw hospitals apart from ambulances, and stop a click on a unit from starting a fake trip. Take the simulate buttons off the dispatcher only once the driver phone is what sends picked up and unavailable.

Use four of them. Skip a subagent. This slice is a known edit in `emergency_flow.dart` and the widget test that taps **Provider accepts**.

**minimal-change-engineer.** The diff stays on the three user buttons: **Provider accepts**, **Provider arrived**, and **Mark job as complete**. Accept, Start job, and Complete job on the provider sign-in stay. Cancel, Call, Chat, and Track stay. The rule is what keeps this from turning into a domestic-flow rewrite.

**state-machine.** The domestic job is already a sequence of screens: searching, assigned, en route, in progress. Those three buttons are the events that advance it, fired from the user tab. The skill is how you check that each event belongs to the provider sign-in before deleting the button, so the user screen does not keep a hidden path into the next state.

**ux-writing.** After the buttons go, those screens are waiting screens. Searching already says it is matching a provider nearby. En route and in progress need one line each so the user can tell that arrival and completion happen on the provider phone. The skill is only for that copy.

**mobile-app-builder.** The work is Flutter, in the existing screen widgets. That rule matches the stack. The senior-developer rule is aimed at Laravel and does not fit.

Update the existing widget test in the same pass. It currently taps **Provider accepts**, so it will fail as soon as that button is gone. Leave two-phone test design for the later slice, when a domestic request actually leaves the phone.

No. A phone and an emulator are two separate installs, and a domestic booking never leaves the phone it was made on. Confirming a plumber on one device leaves it on "Finding a plumber." The other device's provider sign-in only sees its own demo jobs, not that booking.

The user asked:

now i want to make it so that i can test provider and user from different interfaces, so if on one device a user asks for a plumber the other device sees that request. how do i make this "connection" ?

The reply recorded:

Both devices have to talk to the same server. The plumber request has to be saved there, and the provider phone has to read it from there. Right now that never happens.

Confirming a plumber request only changes `domesticJob` to `searching` inside the app on that one phone. The provider screen does not ask the server for work. It opens `incomingRequests`, which starts as `[0]`, and `0` is the first row of `demoRequests`: "Pipe leak repair."

An ambulance request already makes this trip. The phone sends a POST request to `https://madadplus.onrender.com/api/v1/emergency-requests`, the server stores it, and a socket tells the other side. A domestic booking needs the same kind of trip, with one difference: the server waits for a provider to accept it instead of assigning an ambulance itself.

1. On Confirm, the user phone sends a POST request with the trade, the issue, and the place. The screen stays on "Finding a plumber" until the server says a provider accepted.
2. The provider phone, once signed in as a plumber, listens for that new request and shows it in place of "Pipe leak repair." Accept job sends an update for that same request.
3. The user phone receives that update and only then leaves "Finding a plumber."

The emulator and your phone can both reach `https://madadplus.onrender.com`. A server running only on your computer cannot, because the phone is not on that machine. This needs a new domestic request on the backend. Ibad's current API only stores ambulance requests.

The user asked:

now i want to make it so that i can test domestic provider and user from different interfaces, so if on one device a user asks for a plumber the other device sees that request. how do i make this "connection" ?

The reply recorded:

Both devices have to talk to the same server. They never talk to each other. An ambulance request already works this way: the phone sends a POST to `https://madadplus.onrender.com`, and the other screen hears the result over the socket. A plumber request never makes that call. "Pipe leak repair" is only the `demoRequests` list inside the app.

The connection is three steps on that same server.

1. When the user taps Confirm, the phone saves a row: trade, issue, place, and status open. The user screen stays on "Finding a plumber" and listens for that row's id, the same way an ambulance request listens after it is created.
2. The provider phone loads open rows for its trade instead of `demoRequests`. A new row shows up as a job the provider can accept.
3. When the provider taps Accept job, the server marks that row accepted. The user's phone receives that update and leaves "Finding a plumber."

Until that row exists on the server, the emulator and the phone will keep showing different jobs. The backend for this is not in the app, and the current database migration only has `emergency_requests`. Ibad has to add the domestic request on the API before the two phones can share one.

The reply recorded:

Ahmed's push is the commit `dispatcher updates` on `origin/Web`. Your local `Web` already contains it, and it has not been pushed, so GitHub's `Web` is still his. `Webtest` does not have that commit yet.

Merging `Webtest` into `Web` is the direction that would put your test work onto `Web`. Do the opposite: bring `origin/Web` into `Webtest`.

You also have uncommitted edits in `madadplus-web/app.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` while sitting on `Web`. Stash those first so they are not committed on `Web`.

```bat
git stash push -m "dispatcher edits" -- madadplus-web/app.js madadplus-web/index.html madadplus-web/style.css
git checkout Webtest
git merge origin/Web --no-edit
```

That updates `Webtest` only. `Web` and `origin/Web` stay as they are.

Git will stop on all three dispatcher files, because Ahmed changed them and `Webtest` changed them too. For each conflict, keep the part you still want from `Webtest`, keep Ahmed's part, then:

```bat
git add madadplus-web/app.js madadplus-web/index.html madadplus-web/style.css
git commit -m "Merge origin/Web into Webtest"
git stash pop
```

The stash pop puts your uncommitted edits back on `Webtest`. Do not run `git push origin Web`.

The reply recorded:

All of it is doable. The phone and the dispatcher can be built on the branches you already have. A few pieces stay with Ibad, because the live board already calls routes the server does not have.

The driver map shows the hospital pin only after **Picked up**. Until then it shows the user’s pin.

**Ambulance**

Both location options replace the hardcoded DHA pin. **Find my location** uses the phone’s GPS permission. The typed address is turned into a pin with a free OpenStreetMap lookup, the same map the dispatcher already uses. Either way, the request sends a real latitude and longitude.

For speech, use Gemini’s free transcription tier, not Whisper. Google’s pricing page lists Gemini 3.5 Transcribe as free of charge on the free tier, with rate limits, and the paid price is about $0.005 a minute. Whisper is listed at $0.006 a minute. One short clip per request fits a jury demo. The same call can read English or Urdu and return the incident and the number of people. If the quota fails, the user lands on the details form, which you already planned.

The mic button is the first step. If neither field comes back, the popup names both missing fields and opens the details screen empty, with no mic. If only one field comes back, the popup names the missing one and the form is already filled with the other. **What happened** and **people needing help** stay required. Extra details stay optional.

**Dispatcher**

Ambulance markers become a small ambulance drawing, colored green, orange, or red for free, busy, and unavailable. A person who has never seen the board should be able to tell they are ambulances.

One pin goes on each of these places, looked up by name:

- Parklane Hospital
- Clifton Kidney & General Hospital
- South City Hospital
- Infinity Eye Care Centre
- Clifton Hospital
- KKT Orthopedic Spine Center
- Niazi Hospital, Tauheed Commercial
- Medi Life Clinics
- Doctors Plaza, the Plaza

Parklane is near more than one ambulance, so it is still one pin. The pin is a different shape from the ambulance.

Making five ambulances free is Ibad’s job. The board reads the server, and the server’s own word for a free unit is `AVAILABLE`. The board already shows that as Free. He sets five of A-01 through A-07 to `AVAILABLE`.

The drive is the next piece. When a request arrives with coordinates, the dispatcher draws a street route from the free ambulance to that pin and moves the ambulance along it. After the driver taps **Picked up**, the route continues from the user to the chosen hospital. The first half can be drawn on the board once the request has coordinates. The second half starts only when that tap reaches the server. Today the driver screen keeps **Picked up** on the phone, so Ibad has to accept that update.

The **Mark free** popup is the same gap. The button already calls `PATCH /api/v1/ambulances/:id/status`. The server rejects it, and the code comment says `AVAILABLE` is only set inside complete. Ibad adds that status update. The button can stay as it is.

The pulse is a pin at the request’s coordinates with a repeating ring. It appears when the request arrives and goes away when the ambulance reaches the user or the request ends.

**Driver**

The pickup screen still shows a fixed demo address and a fixed medical line. Those have to be the address, incident, and phone number from the request the user just sent. The driver screen loads that request from the server instead of the demo sentence. Then the user’s phone, the board, and the driver show the same call.

The map stays hidden with no active request. When one arrives, it opens on the user’s pin. After **Picked up**, the hospital pin appears. The app chooses among the named hospitals using the incident and the distance, so chest pain does not get sent to the eye centre just because it is closer.

**Domestic provider**

The provider’s inspection charge is stored on the server. The provider sets the number. The user’s list shows that charge next to the rating, and the user picks. Ibad adds the field and the endpoints. The app sends the number and displays it. No payment has to run for the jury to see the choice. If a rating is not already stored for each provider, that number is part of the same API work.

**Real-time test**

An ambulance request can already be tested across devices. The phone posts to `https://madadplus.onrender.com`, and the dispatcher hears it on the socket. The pass is: the phone sends a request, the board marks that unit busy and shows the pulsing pin, and the driver phone shows the same address and incident.

A plumber request cannot do that yet. Confirming one only changes the screen on that phone. Ibad has to add a domestic request on the API before the second phone can see it. The inspection charge belongs on that same request path.

The user asked:

so what do we need to change to connect the backend to the frontend fully with the correct api so that requests from a user will reach the driver/dispatcher/domestic provider without having to hardcode anything? and which agents/skills will be best for this? im not a backend expert so explain in understandable terms

The reply recorded:

The server on `main` can already carry a request. The screens still keep most of it on the phone, so the driver, the dispatcher, and the domestic provider never see it.

Think of the server as the only shared copy. The user’s phone writes the request there. The dispatcher and the driver read that same copy. They do not talk to each other.

## User’s phone

The location screen and the details screen already know the address, what happened, and how many people need help. The send button throws those away. It posts only the pin and `type: "ambulance"`. The server rejects that. It also requires `address`, `description`, and `peopleCount`, and it wants `inputMethod` to be `MANUAL` or `VOICE`.

Send the fields the screens already collected. The reply comes back with a request id and the assigned ambulance. The phone already listens on that request. Keep that.

## Dispatcher

The board on `Webtest` waits for an event called `queue.new`. The server never sends that. It sends `queue.updated`, and that message already includes the address, the pin, what happened, how many people, and which ambulance was assigned.

On open, also load `GET /api/v1/emergency-requests`, so a refresh still shows calls that are in progress.

Two buttons use names Ibad did not use:

- Reassign should be `POST /api/v1/emergency-requests/:id/assign` with `{ ambulanceId }`.
- Bar should be `POST /api/v1/emergency-requests/:id/blocked-ambulances` with `{ ambulanceId }`.
- Mark free already matches `PATCH /api/v1/ambulances/:id/status` with `{ status: "FREE" }`. The error text on that button is out of date.

Hospital pins can come from `GET /api/v1/hospitals`. Those nine places are already stored.

## Driver’s phone

That screen is a local demo. Names like Hal Jordan and the fixed pickup never come from the server.

`GET /api/v1/ambulances` already returns each unit with its driver id and name. The driver picks their own name from that list. Then:

- `GET /api/v1/drivers/:driverId/portal` loads the active call, including the address and what happened.
- The phone joins the `driver` room with that driver id and listens for `request.assigned`.
- **Picked up** calls `PATCH /api/v1/drivers/:driverId/requests/:requestId/pickup`. The server chooses the nearest hospital and sends it back.
- Arriving at the hospital calls `PATCH .../hospital`.

## Domestic

Booking a plumber only changes the screen on that phone. The server already has the other half:

- `GET /api/v1/specialisations` and `GET /api/v1/providers` return the trade, the rating, and the inspection charge.
- Creating a job is `POST /api/v1/domestic-requests` with the provider id, the trade id, the description, and the address.
- The provider’s phone joins the `provider` room, loads `GET /api/v1/providers/:providerId/requests`, and accepts with `PATCH /api/v1/providers/:providerId/requests/:requestId/accept`.
- Changing the inspection charge is `PATCH /api/v1/providers/:providerId/inspection-fee`.

One piece is still missing on the server. A domestic booking also requires a `userId`, and there is no route that tells the phone who the caller is. The seed has a “Demo User,” but the id is created by the database, so it cannot be pasted into the app. Ask Ibad for one lookup, for example by phone number, that returns that user’s id. Everything else for this path already exists.

The screens call `https://madadplus.onrender.com`. This only works live after Render is running commit `ecfe6ef`.

## Who should do it

- `mobile-app-builder` for the user’s phone, the driver phone, and both domestic phones.
- `web-gis-developer` for the dispatcher board, the request pin, and the hospital pins.
- `realtime-collaboration-engineer` for the socket rooms: `dispatch`, `driver`, `request`, and `provider`.
- `api-tester` to check each call against the live server.
- `backend-architect` only for the caller lookup. Leave the rest of `server.js` as Ibad wrote it.

You will know it is connected when one request typed on the user’s phone shows the same address on the dispatcher and on the driver phone, and a plumber booked on one phone shows up on the provider’s phone.

**User phone.** The location and the incident stay on the phone. When it asks for an ambulance it only sends latitude, longitude, and `type: "ambulance"`. The live server rejects that. **Dispatcher.** It already loads the ambulances and listens to the server. A new call is only drawn when the server says `queue.new`. **Domestic.** The whole job stays on one phone: Hal Jordan, DHA Phase 5, an 18 minute ETA. The user list has to come from `GET /api/v1/providers`, including the rating and the inspection fee that provider set. Booking has to call `POST /api/v1/domestic-requests`. The provider phone has to join the `provider` room and accept with the accept route. Setting the fee uses `PATCH /api/v1/providers/:id/inspection-fee`.

## Contract
POST https://madadplus.onrender.com/api/v1/emergency-requests accepts JSON with lat, lng, type: "ambulance", address, description, and peopleCount. peopleCount is a whole number of 1 or more. inputMethod is MANUAL or VOICE. additionalDetails and callerPhone may be omitted. The 4+ chip sends 4. A body with only lat, lng, and type is rejected.

The create response and every later request payload use these fields: requestId, status, phase, type, callerPhone, pickupAddress, pickupLocation {lat, lng}, emergencyDescription, peopleCount, additionalDetails, inputMethod, hospital, hospitalAddress, assignedAmbulance. assignedAmbulance, when present, has id, label, driver {id, name, phone}, and location {lat, lng}. hospital, when present, has id, name, address, and location.

The dispatch socket room receives queue.updated with that payload, and ambulance.updated. It does not receive queue.new. request.pickedUp, request.completed, and request.reassigned go to the request room and the driver room. queue.updated is also sent to the dispatch room for those changes.

Reassign is POST /api/v1/emergency-requests/:requestId/assign with { ambulanceId }.
Barring a unit is POST /api/v1/emergency-requests/:requestId/blocked-ambulances with { ambulanceId }. That call records the block. It does not assign a different ambulance.
Mark free stays PATCH /api/v1/ambulances/:ambulanceId/status with { status: "FREE" }. A BUSY unit returns 409 unless force is true, and force cancels the active request. Do not send force.

GET /api/v1/ambulances returns label, status, lat, lng, driverId, driverName, and driverPhone.
GET /api/v1/hospitals returns id, name, address, lat, and lng.
GET /api/v1/providers returns id, name, status, rating, inspectionFee, specialisationId, and specialisationName.
GET /api/v1/drivers/:driverId/portal returns the driver, the ambulance, and activeRequest in the payload shape above.
Driver actions are PATCH /api/v1/drivers/:driverId/requests/:requestId/pickup, .../hospital, and .../dropoff. Pickup is what attaches the nearest hospital on the server. The phone does not choose the hospital.
The driver socket joins with join:driver and the driver id. The caller socket already joins with join:request.

A domestic booking is POST /api/v1/domestic-requests with userId, providerId, specialisationId, description, and address. userId must already exist in users. There is no users route. Read userId only from --dart-define=DEMO_USER_ID. Do not write an id into source. Provider id and specialisation id come from GET /api/v1/providers. The provider sets a fee with PATCH /api/v1/providers/:providerId/inspection-fee and { inspectionFee }. The provider loads jobs from GET /api/v1/providers/:providerId/requests, joins with join:provider, and accepts with PATCH /api/v1/providers/:providerId/requests/:requestId/accept.
