The reply recorded:

The request was already saved. The phone then treated the next step as a failure, and the countdown closed the call before the driver could pick the patient up.

A second request reused a socket that can only be opened once. The server had already stored the call, so the driver saw the address, while the user was sent back to the confirm screen with "We could not send the emergency request." The first request did not hit that, because the socket was still free.

The same phone also ran a 15-second countdown and then marked the call completed. By the time the driver tapped **Picked up**, the server answered "Request cannot perform pickup from COMPLETED."

Both are fixed. The user phone can open a new request socket each time, and that countdown no longer completes the call. The driver dropoff is what completes it.

Press **R** in both `flutter run` terminals so the phone and the emulator load this code, then send a new request.

can i not stash these?

The reply recorded:

A plain `git stash` leaves those files behind, because they are untracked. Checkout is refusing them for that reason.

Stash only the dispatcher folder, then switch:

```bat
git stash push -u -m "dispatcher on main" -- madadplus-web
git checkout Web
```

The phone folder stays where it is. After the switch, `madadplus-web` is the copy stored on `Web`. To bring this newer dispatcher back, return to `main` and run `git stash pop`.

The user asked:

how do i make some ambulances free? do i need to go to supabase for this?

The reply recorded:

No. Supabase is only the manual override for a unit that is stuck.

An ambulance becomes free when its call ends. On the driver phone, finish the trip with the dropoff slide. The server then sets that unit to `FREE`.

On the dispatcher, **Mark free** works for a unit that is unavailable. A unit that is still `BUSY` is rejected, because it has an open call. The button does not send `force`, and `force` would cancel that call.

Use the Supabase `ambulances` table only when a test call was left open and you want to set `status` to `FREE` by hand.

The user asked:

how do i make some ambulances free on backend? do i need to go to supabase for this?

The reply recorded:

You do not need Supabase. The live API can free a unit, and that also closes the call attached to it.

A unit that is already `FREE` needs nothing. A unit that is `UNAVAILABLE` can be freed from the dispatcher with **Mark free**.

A `BUSY` unit is rejected unless the active call is cancelled. This does that for one ambulance. Replace the id with the one from `GET https://madadplus.onrender.com/api/v1/ambulances`:

```bat
curl -X PATCH "https://madadplus.onrender.com/api/v1/ambulances/THE_AMBULANCE_ID/status" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"status\":\"FREE\",\"force\":true}"
```

`force` cancels that ambulance's current request, then sets it to `FREE`. The next request can be assigned to it.

You can build this now. Do not add a map package.

**Where this stands:** the grey box on the driver screen is a placeholder. The caller countdown uses a drawn block, not a map. `flutter_map` is already in the app and already draws OpenStreetMap on the "where is the emergency" screen.

The server already sends the three points:

1. Ambulance latitude and longitude on the assignment.
2. User pickup latitude and longitude on the request.
3. Hospital latitude and longitude after the driver taps **Picked up**.

The reply recorded:

Not yet. Run `flutter test` first, from the app folder, then `flutter run`.

```bat
cd madad_plus_mobile
flutter test test/widget_test.dart
flutter run
```

1. `flutter test` takes about 1 to 2 minutes. It confirms the 5 files compile and no conflict markers are left.
2. `flutter run` builds the app and installs it on the running emulator. It takes about 3 minutes. The first build can take over 5.
3. If `flutter run` asks which device to use, pick the Tecno_Galaxy emulator.

After install, press Get Started and sign in as driver. You should see the ambulance list, not the DHA Phase 5 pickup.

If `flutter test` fails, paste the first error line and stop there.

Next: run `cd madad_plus_mobile` and `flutter test test/widget_test.dart`.

1. **Typed sentence on the driver screen:** the call data the driver screen receives has no field for the sentence the caller typed. The caller's phone sends it to the server as `additionalDetails`, but `EmergencyCall.fromJson` never reads it back. The only description the driver screen gets is `emergencyDescription`, such as "Injury". The server would have to include `additionalDetails` in the call data before the app can show it.
2. **Mark as unavailable during a trip:** there is no request that hands a trip to another ambulance. The only driver request the app sends is `PATCH /api/v1/drivers/{driverId}/requests/{requestId}/{action}`, and only for pickup, hospital and drop-off. The app does listen for a `request.reassigned` message from the server, but nothing sends a reassignment or picks the next ambulance. So the button still shows only when there is no active call.

(tf) C:\Users\Zain Ul Ibad\Desktop\projects\FYP>git show main:docs/driver-reassignment.md
# Driver emergency request contract

## Driver request data

`GET /api/v1/drivers/{driverId}/portal` returns the active call in `activeRequest`.
The same request shape is sent in driver and request-room socket events. Relevant
fields are:

- `additionalDetails`: the caller's free-text details (for example, "I am burnt").
- `pickupLocation`: the caller's original location.
- `dispatchLocation`: the destination for the current leg. Use this for navigation;
  during `phase: "TRANSFER"`, it is the stranded ambulance's latest location.
- `phase`: `PICKUP`, `TRANSFER`, or `HOSPITAL`.
- `hospital.location`: the hospital destination when available.

## Change ambulance

Use this when the current ambulance cannot continue:

```http
PATCH /api/v1/drivers/{driverId}/requests/{requestId}/reassign
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "reason": "Vehicle breakdown",
  "lat": 24.8607,
  "lng": 67.0011
}
```

`lat` and `lng` are optional, but must be sent together. If omitted, the server
uses the ambulance's last saved location. The endpoint verifies that the request
is currently assigned to this driver's ambulance, marks that ambulance
`UNAVAILABLE`, then chooses the nearest free, unblocked ambulance.

For a call still in `PICKUP`, the replacement is dispatched to the caller's
`pickupLocation` and receives the caller details, including `additionalDetails`.
After pickup, the replacement is dispatched to the current ambulance location;
the request enters `TRANSFER` until the replacement confirms pickup.

Successful response:

```json
{
  "ambulanceId": "old-ambulance-id",
  "status": "UNAVAILABLE",
  "replacementRequestId": "request-id",
  "reassignmentStatus": "ASSIGNED",
  "callerMessage": "Your ambulance has changed to A-02.",
  "request": {
    "requestId": "request-id",
    "status": "TRANSFER_EN_ROUTE",
    "phase": "TRANSFER",
    "pickupLocation": { "lat": 24.86, "lng": 67.00 },
    "dispatchLocation": { "lat": 24.87, "lng": 67.01 },
    "additionalDetails": "I am burnt",
    "assignedAmbulance": { "id": "new-ambulance-id", "label": "A-02" }
  }
}
```

If no free ambulance is available, the request is still successful but
`reassignmentStatus` is `QUEUED`, `request.assignedAmbulance` is `null`, and
`callerMessage` says a replacement is being found. A mismatched driver/request
returns `404`; a request in a non-reassignable state returns `409`.

## Socket events

Join `request:{requestId}` to receive caller updates. When reassigned, the server
emits `request.reassigned` with the request fields above, plus
`reassignmentStatus` and `callerMessage`. If no replacement is free yet, it emits
`request.queued` with the same message fields. The newly assigned driver also
receives `request.reassigned` in `driver:{driverId}`.

For the second fix, I'm designing a `reassignDriverRequest` method that takes a driver ID, request ID, and optional coordinates, returning a `DriverReassignment` object. I'm working through the body logic, only encoding lat/lng when both are present, and reasoning carefully about which fields should be nullable (like replacementRequestId and callerMessage) since the contract doesn't fully specify behavior for the QUEUED case, trying to stay faithful to what's documented rather than inventing structure.

That means loosening `_SecondaryButton.onPressed` from `VoidCallback` to a nullable type, which is a safe, backward-compatible change to that shared widget.

For the confirmation flow, I'm writing a `confirmUnavailable` method that shows a dialog and, if confirmed, calls `reassignDriverRequest`, checking `mounted` afterward. The dialog copy warns that the ambulance becomes unavailable and the nearest free one takes the call, with Cancel/Confirm actions.

For testing, I need a fake service that records reassign calls with their coordinates and can simulate failures (404/409 ApiExceptions), then verify the button labels and behavior across pickup and to-hospital states.

I'm covering the cancel path (no reassign call, status stays BUSY), the success path (reassign fires, status flips to UNAVAILABLE, call clears, toggle label updates), and the error paths where status and call persist with an error message shown. I also want to verify lat/lng are omitted from the request body when the ambulance has no coordinates, and include a separate case with coordinates present to confirm they're sent correctly.

For the socket fix, I'm adding an optional onCallerMessage callback to the connect method, and splitting the existing event handling so request.assigned keeps its current parsing behavior while request.queued only extracts the caller message without running fromJson, since the caller can only receive a queued event after an initial assignment.

I'll also handle request.reassigned similarly, extracting just the message string when present. On the state side, I'm adding a callerMessage field that gets set via the callback, triggers notifyListeners, and gets cleared on reset or when a new request starts.

For the UI, I'm adding an "Ambulance update" info card that shows the caller message across the Assigned, EnRoute, Approaching, and Arrived screens, matching the existing dispatch update card style.

For the Fix 3 test, I need to update the test's SilentSocketService mock to capture the onCallerMessage callback so I can trigger it manually, then figure out how to get the test into an emergencyAssigned connected state to verify the behavior.

Better idea: make the private caller-message handler public, matching the existing pattern of `receivePickup`, so tests can invoke it directly. That way a test can call `session.state.receiveCallerMessage(...)` with a sample message and verify it shows up as expected.

Since the real socket service relies on live sockets and can't be unit tested directly, I could pull the raw data parsing logic into a standalone function like `callerMessageFrom(dynamic data)` within the socket service, so it's testable in isolation without needing a server connection.

I'd test cases where the map has a message, lacks one, is blank, isn't a map, or resembles a queued request payload without requestId/status, confirming the helper doesn't depend on fromJson. I also need to add `onCallerMessage` as a parameter to the fake's connect override, since overriding with fewer optional params would break compilation. Separately, I'm flagging a question about the TRANSFER_EN_ROUTE status, the receiving driver sees a "Picked up" pickup title, but the contract description of TRANSFER state until replacement confirmation seems worth double-checking against this behavior.

I'm noting that `dispatchLocation` and `phase` aren't parsed by EmergencyCall, so during a TRANSFER the receiving driver's map points to the caller's original location instead of the stranded ambulance, worth reporting but not fixing. Similarly, unknown TRANSFER-prefixed statuses beyond TRANSFER_EN_ROUTE would fall back to a generic "Active call" screen with no actions, which I'll flag. I also want to verify there's no `reason` field in the contract, confirm the SDK version, and run the widget test suite without touching the server or committing anything, no backend-architect needed since there's no server-side change here.

I'm mapping out the driver state machine around reassignment: pickup/hospital leg busy with an active call, tapping the button opens a confirm dialog, cancel returns, confirm triggers a loading state with disabled buttons, success resets to idle/unavailable, and failure leaves the state unchanged while showing the driverError message, gated by driverCall, driverId, and not already loading. I've confirmed the `_ErrorNotice` widget already renders driverError correctly and that it clears on next load, so that's fine. I also checked that `ApiException` already supports an optional statusCode parameter without breaking existing call sites or test usage. Check out `Web` (or `Webtest`) and restore the stashed hospital-pin changes from `v4.1` to finish the first open dispatcher item (about 5 minutes).

## Done

### Mobile: Ambulance
1. Replaced the hardcoded DHA pin with **Find my location** and a typed address.
2. Shows the chosen place as a pin on the map.
3. Sends that latitude and longitude with the request.
4. Added the circular mic button before the details form using Gemini’s free transcription tier (`gemini-3.5-transcribe` / `gemini-3.5-flash`) for English (`en-US`) and Urdu (`ur-PK`).
5. Fills what happened and people needing help from the speech.
6. Shows a popup naming both missing fields and opens the details form empty (with no mic) when neither comes back.
7. Shows a popup naming the single missing field and keeps the understood field when only one comes back.
8. Keeps what happened and people needing help required, and extra details optional.

### Mobile: Ambulance driver
1. Shows the address, incident, additional details, and phone number from the user’s live request.
2. Keeps the map hidden (grey pin placeholder) until a request arrives.
3. Shows the map with the user’s pin and a straight-line route when a request arrives *(Future work: replace the straight-line polyline with road-accurate routing)*.
4. Shows the hospital pin and straight-line route after **Picked up** *(Future work: road-accurate routing)*.
5. Sends **Picked up** (`PATCH /api/v1/drivers/:driverId/requests/:requestId/pickup`) to the server so the hospital leg starts.

### Backend (`main` branch and live Render)
1. Stores the request’s address, latitude, longitude, incident, people count, input method, and additional details.
2. Added `PATCH /api/v1/ambulances/:ambulanceId/status` so **Mark free** sets `FREE`.
3. Seeded five of `A-01` through `A-07` (`A-01`, `A-02`, `A-04`, `A-05`, `A-06`) as `FREE` in `seeds/demo_data.js`.
4. Accepts **Picked up** from the driver and transitions the trip to the hospital leg.
5. Added `POST /api/v1/domestic-requests`, `GET /api/v1/providers/:providerId/requests`, and `PATCH .../accept` so a user can create a job and a provider can see and accept it.
6. Stores each provider’s inspection charge (`PATCH /api/v1/providers/:providerId/inspection-fee`).
7. Stores a rating for each provider in the `providers` table.

### Dispatcher (`Web` branch)
1. Draws each unit as an ambulance icon colored for `FREE` (green), `BUSY` (amber), and `UNAVAILABLE` (red).

## Yet to do

*(Note: the code for Domestic services and Domestic provider is already wired in `madad_plus_mobile`, but listed here since you haven't tested/touched the provider flow yet.)*

### Mobile: Domestic services & Domestic provider
1. Verify showing each provider’s rating and inspection charge on the trade screen.
2. Seed a second provider per trade in `seeds/demo_data.js` so the user chooses between two providers per trade (currently 1 Plumber, 1 Electrician, and 1 AC Technician are seeded).
3. Verify sending the domestic request to the server and seeing it arrive on the provider’s phone (`test-scenario` two-phone pass).
4. Verify letting the provider set and save their inspection charge on the server.

### Backend (live Render state)
1. Reset live Render ambulances so five of `A-01` through `A-07` are `FREE` right now (live Render currently has only `A-04` and `A-05` `FREE` from earlier test runs).

### Dispatcher (`Web` / `Webtest` branch)
1. Commit the 9 hospital pins (`GET /api/v1/hospitals`) onto `Web` (this was coded in `v4.1` and sits in `stash@{2}`, not on `Web`).
2. Pulse a pin at the user’s `pickupLocation` coordinates when `queue.new` / `queue.updated` arrives.
3. Move the assigned ambulance along a street route to the user’s pin.
4. Continue the route from the user’s pin to the chosen hospital’s `hospital.location` after `request.pickedUp`.

## Cannot do yet

### 1. Choose the hospital using both the incident and the distance (Mobile driver / Backend)
* **Why it cannot be done yet (`workflow-architect` Spec vs. Reality gap):**
  * **Missing data column:** The `hospitals` table in `migrations/20261002120000_expand_madadplus_scope.js` only has `id`, `name`, `phone`, `address`, `location`, and `active`. There is no column or mapping for which incidents (`Cardiac`, `Accident`, `Injury`, `Medical`) each hospital handles.
  * **Distance-only query:** In `src/server.js`, `markDriverRequest(..., "pickup")` selects a hospital using only PostGIS distance (`ORDER BY location <-> pickup_location LIMIT 1`) and ignores `emergency_description`.
* **How to do it (`workflow-architect` & `workflow-optimizer`):**
  1. **Define the incident-to-hospital mapping rule:** Add a `supported_incidents` array column (or a lookup map in `src/server.js`) mapping `Cardiac`, `Accident`, `Injury`, and `Medical` to the 9 seeded hospitals.
  2. **Update the `pickup` transition in `src/server.js`:** Filter active hospitals by the request’s `emergency_description` first, then order by `location <-> pickup_location`, falling back to nearest overall if no specialty match is active.
  3. **Verify the handoff contract:** `PATCH /api/v1/drivers/:driverId/requests/:requestId/pickup` already returns `hospital: { id, name, address, location }`, so the mobile app and dispatcher will automatically receive the incident-matched hospital without mobile code changes.

### 2. Move the dispatcher ambulance along a street route to the user and then to the hospital (Dispatcher)
* **Why it cannot be done yet (`workflow-architect` Handoff Contract & State gaps):**
  * **Intentional guard in `madadplus-web/app.js`:** Line 9 states the board *"never invents a booking, a destination, or a movement animation itself"* and only moves markers when `ambulance.updated` fires.
  * **No street-routing service or live GPS stream:** Neither the mobile driver app nor `src/server.js` calls a road-routing API (like OSRM) or streams step-by-step street coordinates over `ambulance.updated`.
* **How to do it (`workflow-architect` & `workflow-optimizer`):**
  1. **Add a road-route handoff contract:** On `queue.new` / `queue.updated` (when `status` is `ASSIGNED` or `EN_ROUTE`), have `madadplus-web/app.js` request a driving geometry from OSRM (`https://router.project-osrm.org/route/v1/driving/{ambLng},{ambLat};{pickupLng},{pickupLat}?overview=full&geometries=geojson`) and draw the street `L.polyline`.
  2. **Automate the marker step loop (`workflow-optimizer`):** Interpolate the ambulance marker along the returned GeoJSON coordinate array on a timer until `request.pickedUp` arrives, with a straight-line fallback if OSRM times out (5s timeout).
  3. **Chain the hospital leg on `request.pickedUp`:** When `queue.updated` / `request.pickedUp` arrives with `hospital.location`, clear the pickup polyline, fetch the OSRM route from `pickupLocation` to `hospital.location`, and step the ambulance marker to the hospital until `request.completed`.

Restart the app and open Get started. These are the skill rules that actually changed those five screens, and the ones that were left alone.

## What changed

1. **Press feedback.** Get started, Continue, Verify, the four sign-in links, and the two home cards scale to 0.97 the moment a finger goes down, then ease back in 100ms. If the phone has reduced motion on, that scale is skipped.
2. **Type.** Large titles use tighter letter-spacing and tighter line-height. Body text on these screens uses a looser line-height. The bar titles (Welcome, Sign in, Verify phone, Karachi, DHA Phase 5) are dark and a bit lighter in weight.
3. **Materials.** The page behind these screens is the grouped gray. The sign-in links sit in one white group. The phone field is filled, with rounded corners. The code boxes and the two home cards use a soft shadow. Each icon sits in a tinted rounded plate. The home tab bar is a blurred translucent layer with a light top edge.
4. **Grouping.** The four account links are one group, in the same order, with the same words. The home cards lost the thick colored outline. The icon color still marks emergency versus a local service.

## What the skill covers that these screens did not need

1. **Drag, flick, and springs.** Nothing on these screens is dragged, swiped, or thrown. There is no sheet, no rubber-band edge, and no velocity to hand off. The press uses the skill's short ease-out, not a spring.
2. **Screen transitions.** Moving from splash to welcome to sign-in is still an instant swap. Enter and exit along the same path would matter if a panel slid in. These screens do not.
3. **Sound and haptics.** The skill says to add those only for a real commit, snap, or error. A tap through Get started does not have one.
4. **Reduced transparency and higher contrast.** This Flutter version has no reduced-transparency flag, so the home bar always blurs. A high-contrast solid border was not added.
5. **A new font, and animated glass.** GeneralSans stayed. The blur does not grow in as the bar appears. Scroll does not fade under the header, because the header is not floating over moving content.

The reply recorded:

Storage goes in the state class, and the GPS steps move there so Find my location and the picker share one path.

I'm noticing the service location screen also has its own "Find my location" feature, but the plan is to leave that untouched and only refactor the emergency screen's device location logic. For the locate function, I'm designing it to return a record containing coordinates and address, or throw a descriptive error if it fails.

I'm weighing whether throwing plain strings is bad practice versus wrapping in an Exception versus returning a nullable record with a separate error field -- trying to avoid overly complex tuple types while keeping the API simple enough for screens to consume.

For tests, I need to remember to mock SharedPreferences' initial values in setUp since the constructor loads data without awaiting, otherwise it'll throw an unhandled async error. I'm also sketching storage format -- a JSON list under a 'homePlaces' key plus a separate key tracking the selected address -- and planning the picker screen's layout with an address text field and an action button to confirm the selection.

For the GPS button I'll label it 'Find my location' for consistency between screens, add a 'SAVED LOCATIONS' section with existing row components, and include empty-state text and error display. For the home title, I want to make it tappable when onTitle is provided by wrapping it in an InkWell with a small expand_more chevron icon for discoverability, plus proper semantics, while switching that bit of state access from read to watch.

Using watch is fine for the build context. For the location action, I'll treat 'Use my current location' as a secondary-styled button beneath the emergency action, checking if a home pin exists before dropping a new one, otherwise showing the error message. Now I need to find the constructor to wire in the call that loads saved home pins on init.

Writing persistence logic...

I'm weighing whether to drop the try/catch entirely since tests mock the plugin and errors would otherwise just hit the zone handler silently. There's also a subtle race to consider: if loadHomePlaces runs in the constructor while a test seeds data via saveHomePlace before the load finishes, I need to check whether that causes duplicate entries.

Writing save logic...

For deduping, I should match by address rather than full record equality, removing any existing entry with the same address before inserting the new one at the front. Selecting a home place should just update the chosen key and notify listeners, with navigation back handled by the screen rather than the state object.

Run these three commands from the repo folder. You are on `Web` right now, so this is safe to run as-is.

```
git checkout Web
git branch -D Webtest
git checkout -b Webtest
```

`Web` is commit `735d0f7`, which is the dispatcher in the first screenshot. `Webtest` is commit `5ff3c06` (`eh`), and it tracks `origin/Webtest` at that same old commit. Deleting the local branch and running `git checkout Webtest` checks that remote branch out again, so you get the second screenshot. `git checkout -b Webtest` makes a new branch from the `Web` you are on.

Restart the server on port 5500 after the checkout, then hard refresh the browser.

Do not push `Webtest` yet. A normal push will be rejected, and a force push would replace the remote `eh` commit.

I notice the pickup leg stalled at 24.82083, short of the actual pickup point at 24.8235, while the toHospital leg never moved at all, likely because OSRM snaps the route endpoint to the nearest road point rather than the exact coordinate, so the route finished early.

Yet pickupDone didn't flip true until roughly 35 seconds in, not right when the route completed around 10s, leaving a 25-second stall with no movement. That delay doesn't match the expected time-based animation logic, so something else, maybe a snapshot reconciliation step, is likely holding things up before the hospital leg's route fetch even begins.

This points elsewhere, maybe the real issue is with ticking logic. Checking syncAmbulanceSnapshot, it skips when no animation exists, which seems fine, but the hospital leg appears to end at the pickup point after only ~6 seconds, suggesting the leg completion logic is terminating prematurely rather than running the full duration.

Tracing why: after PICKED_UP, syncRequestAnimation should transition patientAboard into the hospital leg and fetch a fresh OSRM route from pickup to hospital, but it finishes in 6 seconds with zero movement, so maybe my earlier manual cancelAnimation call on the pickup leg interfered, since that onComplete handler itself kicks off the next leg automatically.

Cardiac, Accident, Injury, and Medical are the wrong set. They are not the same kind of choice, and the caller can tap only one. A rickshaw crash with a broken leg is both an accident and an injury. A heart problem is both cardiac and medical. A burn, a fall, or a beating has no honest chip. Rescue 1122 does not file those as one parent category. Its daily table keeps Medical, Road Traffic Crashes, Falls/Slip, Burn Cases, and Delivery Cases on separate rows ([rescue.gov.pk/AvgReport.aspx](https://www.rescue.gov.pk/AvgReport.aspx)).

If two chips seem true, use this order:

1. A vehicle was involved: Road accident, even if the person is bleeding.
2. The person is hurt, bleeding, or burned, and no vehicle was involved: Hurt or burned.
3. Chest pain, trouble breathing, or they will not wake, with no crash and no wound: Chest pain, breathing, or unconscious.
4. Labour, poisoning, a seizure, stroke signs in someone who is awake, or you do not know: Other or not sure.

That order follows the dispatch rule that a crash is recorded as the crash, even when the person is also hurt ([IAED Journal, Mechanism of Injury](https://www.iaedjournal.org/mechanism-of-injury)). The Karachi ambulance page names road traffic accidents, cardiac emergencies, and obstetric emergencies as separate jobs ([SIEHS](https://www.siehs.org/2025/06/free-ambulance-service-in-sindh/)). Chest pain stays on the chip because "cardiac" asks the caller to diagnose. Labour stays under Other or not sure because this screen is one tap, and the details box can say "labour."

[Grok incident chips](21961267-b541-43b9-b68b-08743d56e3c2) is the base. [Judge incident chip sets](82546672-3156-4acf-b2e7-a9650384180f) agreed, because only that set tells the caller which chip wins. The fourth label takes "or not sure" from [Terra incident chips](35886b65-ffd0-4a63-a42d-a1fdd64e0182). [Sonnet incident chips](80a8787c-b545-4ff9-b8f3-1ccd33f2f531) wanted six chips, including a separate Burn and Pregnancy. Those were rejected. "Accident or injury" puts the overlap back on the screen.

The details screen is unchanged.

For the driver screens, I'm softening "no caller phone was sent" into "the caller didn't share a phone number," and "the server did not attach a hospital address" into "no hospital address came with this call," while leaving test-checked strings like "slide to the end to confirm" untouched. I'm writing the translucent card background styling...

_FlowFrame stays as is. Now I'm implementing the press-scale spring animation using an unbounded animation controller that tracks a 0-to-1 press value, settling toward targets with a critically damped spring simulation triggered on pointer down/up events.

On build, the animated builder reduces opacity slightly when reduced motion is preferred, or otherwise scales the child down subtly based on the press value. I need to double-check whether SpringSimulation requires importing the physics library separately or if it's already covered by flutter/animation.dart.

Still adding import safeguards...

The drag handler needs to stop any return animation and update slide state directly, and for reduced-motion I'll just snap the slider straight to 0 instead of animating.

I'm defining two spring constants, one tuned for press feedback with higher stiffness, another softer one for the slider's return motion using a 0.3s response time. flutter run -d emulator-5554 --dart-define=DEMO_USER_ID=

It does not send the final total. The customer Accept and Refuse screen stays as it is, so the customer still sees one repair total plus the inspection fee.

Write new labels in the same plain voice as the existing lines. Use "Parts total: Rs. N" and "Final total: Rs. N". Run the label wording through the humanizer rule.

## Scope
Work only in:
- madad_plus_mobile/lib/emergency_flow.dart
- madad_plus_mobile/lib/services/emergency_request_state.dart
- madad_plus_mobile/test/widget_test.dart

Do not edit lib/services/emergency_service.dart. Do not add a dependency. Do not commit.

## Constraints
Match the file's style: camelCase, and no space before the parenthesis in if, while, and for. Use the existing _ActionButton, _SecondaryButton, _InfoCard, and InputDecoration. Do not add an add-row button. Do not keep Navigate to customer, Call customer, the check icon, or the pin placeholder on these two provider screens. If _MapBlock has no remaining caller, delete it. Leave the ambulance flow and the domestic customer booking flow alone.

## Acceptance criteria
- Accept job shows the address, the problem, the extra note when description has more than one " · " piece, and Start job. It does not show "Customer notified".
- Start job opens Provider notes, Upload photos, and Complete job, and the customer state moves to in progress.
- The provider cost screen has no Repair total field, shows the inspection fee above three component and price rows, shows the parts total under the prices, and shows the final total under that.
- A filled example of prices 100 and 250 with an inspection fee of 2500 submits quotedTotal 350 and shows a final total of 2850.
- flutter test test/widget_test.dart passes.

## Action boundaries
Inspect and edit the three files above, then run the widget tests. Stop and ask before deleting any file other than an unused _MapBlock, before adding a dependency, and before changing the quotedTotal the server receives.

Skills attached with this message: i-have-adhd

The reply recorded:

In the emulator's Device Manager, set that phone's graphics to Hardware, give it 4 CPU cores and 4096 MB of RAM, then cold-boot it.

The log shows the emulator dropping the first frames, not a hang inside the app. The first launch skipped 1,968 frames and took 12 seconds to draw. The second skipped 3,567 frames and took 21 seconds. `Width is zero` is the window before the screen exists. The Gradle and Java warnings are not the lag. `vendor.mesa.virtgpu.kumquat` being denied means this API 36 image (`gphone16k`) is rendering through a slow virtual GPU.

1. Close every other emulator. Two phones at once is what makes this one stall.
2. Edit the AVD: Graphics = Hardware, 4 cores, 4096 MB RAM. Cold boot.
3. If it is still that slow, make a new phone on API 34 or 35. Keep this API 36 image only if you still need it.
4. From `madad_plus_mobile`, run `flutter run --profile -d emulator-5554`. Profile skips the debug overhead that adds to those skipped frames.

Next: cold-boot that phone with Hardware graphics, then run the profile command.

The reply recorded:

`node_modules` is the folder of installed Node packages. On `Webtest` it held the local server's libraries: Express, Socket.IO, Knex, and Postgres.

The dispatcher does not need it. `madadplus-web` is plain HTML and JavaScript, served with `python -m http.server`. The phone app does not need it either. Flutter uses its own packages from `pubspec.yaml`.

You only need `node_modules` if you start the Node server on this computer. The live API is already on Render.

The reply recorded:

I'm noticing the animation jumps at start because pointAtFraction(0) resolves to the route's first point, which isn't the ambulance's actual current position but rather the "from" location used when fetchRoute was called in driveAmbulanceTo, likely the ambulance's original spawn position rather than its live coordinates.

I'm checking whether a periodic sync guard could still let this slip through, since the trace shows currentRequestId set at the jump, but then I wonder if loadAmbulances rebuilds the ambulance objects from scratch with currentRequestId reset to null, which would bypass the guard entirely. Though if that were the case, upsertAmbulanceMarker should have logged a jump when it called setLatLng with the stale position, and no such jump appears in the trace, so that theory doesn't quite hold either.

So maybe amb.lat itself was never actually updated during the pickup leg's animation step, even though the marker displayed correctly, which would mean the discrepancy is between the stored coordinate and the rendered position, not a guard failure at all.

The user asked:

question: why is there @madadplus-web/ in the mobiletest branch, and @madad_plus_mobile/ folder in the Webtest branch? that makes no sense...

The reply recorded:

`madadplus-web` is on `mobiletest` because you committed it today in `f1e7a28` ("uh"). That commit added the dispatcher files: `app.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, and the icons.

`madad_plus_mobile` is not on `Webtest`. That branch tracks zero files from that folder. The phone files you saw there were left in the working folder by the failed stash pop. Git showed them as unmerged, and they were never committed to `Webtest`.

The user asked:

no i mean why are they ON that branch in the first place?

The reply recorded:

`madadplus-web` is on `mobiletest` because that folder was sitting in the project while `mobiletest` was the checked-out branch, and commit `f1e7a28` ("uh", 10:20 PM) recorded it there. Git stores whatever you add on the branch you are on. It does not keep the dispatcher on `Webtest` by itself.

The folder was in the project so the map could run from the same place as the phone. The earlier instruction was not to commit it. The "uh" commit did.

`madad_plus_mobile` is still not on `Webtest`. No commit on that branch contains it. The phone files showed up only in the working folder, left there by the failed stash pop while `Webtest` was checked out.

The user asked:

you're not getting my point: forget commits, why is the mobile folder on the web branch, and why is the web folder on the mobile branch?  yes the mobile folder isnt committed on the web branch but why are they there? what happens if i delete @madad_plus_mobile/ from Webtest branch and @madadplus-web/ from mobiletest?

The reply recorded:

There is one project folder on disk. Checking out a branch only swaps the files that the branch tracks. It does not keep a separate copy of each branch.

`madadplus-web` is in that folder on `mobiletest` because that branch now tracks it. Checkout writes every tracked file to disk, so the dispatcher appears whenever `mobiletest` is checked out.

`madad_plus_mobile` is in that folder on `Webtest` because checkout leaves files alone when the branch does not track them. The phone app's build leftovers, and the file left by the failed stash pop, stayed on disk after the switch. `Webtest` does not contain them.

Deleting `madadplus-web` while `mobiletest` is checked out removes it from disk and Git marks those files deleted. The next checkout of `mobiletest` puts the folder back, unless you commit that deletion. `Webtest` still has its own dispatcher either way.

Deleting `madad_plus_mobile` while `Webtest` is checked out only removes those leftovers. `Webtest` does not change. The next checkout of `mobiletest` puts the phone app back.

The user asked:

whats the difference between flutter run -d and flutter run -d --profile?

Skills attached with this message: i-have-adhd

The reply recorded:

`flutter run -d emulator-5554` builds a debug app. `flutter run --profile -d emulator-5554` builds a profile app, which is the one to use when you want to judge speed.

Debug is the everyday run. Hot reload works, the red DEBUG banner shows, and the app is slower than the one you would ship.

Profile is compiled closer to a release build, so scrolling and startup are nearer to the real app. The DEBUG banner is gone, and hot reload is off. Flutter still allows performance tracing in this mode.

Put `--profile` before `-d`. The command `flutter run -d --profile` treats `--profile` as the device name and fails.

Next: run `flutter run --profile -d emulator-5554` when you want to check speed. Use the command without `--profile` when you want hot reload.

The user asked:

my next idea is to give each service provider their own location, a real life location. before i do that, do i need to add their coordinates/location at the backend, the way we did for the ambulances? how did we store the addresses for the ambulances' current location? and is it translatable for the domestic providers?

Skills attached with this message: i-have-adhd

The reply recorded:

Yes. Add each provider's coordinates on the backend before the app work. `ProviderRow` has no location field, so the phone has nowhere to read one from.

Ambulance current location is a coordinate pair, not a street address. The `ambulances` table stores it as a PostGIS point, `geography(Point, 4326)`, in the `location` column. That column is required, and it has a spatial index. The API returns it as `{ lat, lng }` on `location`. The driver list uses flat `lat` and `lng`. When a driver marks the ambulance unavailable, the phone sends only `{ lat, lng }` to the reassign route. No address text goes with that update.

Street addresses are a separate pair of fields. A pickup has `pickupAddress` plus a `pickupLocation` point. A hospital has an `address` string plus a `location` point.

The same point type works for a domestic provider. The provider record would gain a `location` point and return `{ lat, lng }`, the way an ambulance does. A fixed shop is closer to the hospital shape: keep the address text and the point together. The address already saved on a domestic booking is the customer's job address, and that request does not store coordinates.

Next: say whether each provider's location is a fixed shop, or a point that moves during a job.

The user asked:

each provider's location is a fixed shop, but the provider itself can move to reach a user's location.

dont make any changes on your own till i tell you to, btw

The reply recorded:

Say the word when you want the shop point added. No files were changed.

The shop is a fixed place on the provider record: an address plus a coordinate point, the same pair a hospital already has. The provider can leave that shop and move toward the customer's booking address. That moving position is a separate point, the same kind the ambulance updates with `lat` and `lng`.

Next: reply "add the shop location" when you want that backend change.

Verified path, not a diagnosis:
- The caller socket listens for request.pickedUp in madad_plus_mobile/lib/services/emergency_socket_service.dart and calls receivePickup.
- receivePickup is in madad_plus_mobile/lib/services/emergency_request_state.dart. If the hospital name or address is empty, it returns without starting a route. If both are present, it opens EmergencyScreen.emergencyArrived and calls startRouteLeg with leg 2, from the pickup to the hospital.
- startRouteLeg clears the route when any coordinate is null. Otherwise it stores the two ends, starts a 50ms timer, and calls notifyListeners on each tick until routeProgress reaches 1.
- _EmergencyArrivedScreen in madad_plus_mobile/lib/emergency_flow.dart builds _TripMap. _TripMap places the ambulance with _pointAlongRoute(points, state.routeProgress()) and then calls _mapController.move to that point.
- _pointAlongRoute already subtracts segments[i] before the next segment. Do not rewrite that subtraction.

The hospital name is visible in the screenshot, so the empty-name return is not what that frame shows. A route line is also visible, so the coordinates were present for that frame. The icon still has to be able to stop on a later run.

Run the call once more with the caller's network off when the driver presses Picked up. This tests the one cause the code allows, and no log so far has covered it.

1. Start a call so the caller shows "En route".
2. In a second terminal, turn the caller's network off:
   ```
   adb -s emulator-5554 shell svc wifi disable
   adb -s emulator-5554 shell svc data disable
   ```
   If the emulator ignores these, use airplane mode from its quick settings.
3. Press Picked up on the driver phone.
4. Wait 5 seconds, then turn the network back on:
   ```
   adb -s emulator-5554 shell svc wifi enable
   adb -s emulator-5554 shell svc data enable
   ```
5. Paste the caller's `[van check]` lines.

Success is no `picked up arrived` line and the van parked at the pickup point after leg 1 finishes. That is the "not moving" you saw in the demo.

This run, with the early press, still moved. Picked up arrived at 86% of leg 1. Leg 2 started, the road route arrived with 10 points, and the van drove to 24.80591, 67.03686 near Niazi Hospital (24.8062, 67.0368). Nothing failed. That is two runs without a repro.

Why the offline test is worth running, from the code:

- `connect()` in `emergency_socket_service.dart` supports `onDisconnected` and `onReconnected`, but `_connectToRequest` in `emergency_request_state.dart` passes neither.
- `EmergencyService` has no call that reads a request's current status. The caller learns about Picked up only from the live `request.pickedUp` event.
- A socket drop at the wrong moment would lose that event for good. The van would stop at the pickup point and never start leg 2. I have not proven this happened in the demo. It is the only path in the code that fits.

Two smaller things from the log:

- **Missing lines:** the paste cuts out between 62% and 81% of leg 2 and breaks mid-word ("e van at"). That looks like the terminal, not the app. The van positions on both sides of the gap match the clock.
- **Snap:** on the early press the van jumped from 24.80558 to 24.80682, about 140 m, to the pickup point, then drove to the hospital. I can look at smoothing that separately.

No code changed this turn, and the temporary prints are still in.

Next: the offline run above, about 4 minutes.

I confirm nobody wires up onDisconnected/onReconnected, and there's no GET endpoint for callers to poll request status. So if a `request.pickedUp` event gets dropped during a socket disconnect, it's lost forever, the caller stays stuck at the end of leg 1, never seeing the ambulance arrive, which matches what's shown in the second demo screenshot.

This is a plausible but unproven cause. To actually prove it, I'd want the user to run a quick test: disable the caller emulator's network briefly right as the driver taps "Picked up," then re-enable it, and confirm the caller never advances past that step.

A proper fix would need the caller to re-sync request status after reconnecting, but I don't know if the server even exposes a GET endpoint for request status, I should flag that as unverified rather than assume. I also want to separately note the van's ~140m position jump at pickup, since the user's already expressed dislike for that kind of teleporting behavior on the dispatcher side.

For the actual test, I'll lay out numbered steps: start a call so the caller shows En route, then on the caller's emulator disable wifi and data via adb (`svc wifi disable`, `svc data disable`). I believe these commands work on standard emulators, but since the user asked me not to assume things I haven't verified, I should be upfront that I'm giving my best expectation rather than something I've confirmed in this environment.

Then after pressing picked up on the driver side, wait a few seconds and re-enable wifi and data, watching the caller's van-check lines to confirm no spurious "picked up arrived" line and the van stopping correctly at pickup. I'll note this should take about four minutes total, and close with a concise "next step" line pointing to this offline test.

The code matches this result. The server emits `request.pickedUp` once to whoever is in the room at that moment. `join:request` only joins the room. It does not send the current status. The caller socket can take an `onReconnected` callback, but `_connectToRequest` never passes one, and the app never calls `GET /api/v1/emergency-requests/:requestId`. That GET already returns the same payload as the socket event, including the hospital. A drop across the emit loses Picked up for good, and turning Wi‑Fi back on does not recover it.

The caller now reloads the request when its socket comes back, and starts the hospital drive if pickup already happened. Restart the caller app so this code is running, then repeat the Wi‑Fi test.

While the caller says "En route", turn its network off, press Picked up on the driver phone, wait about 5 seconds, and turn the network back on:

```
adb -s emulator-5554 shell svc wifi disable
adb -s emulator-5554 shell svc data disable
```

```
adb -s emulator-5554 shell svc wifi enable
adb -s emulator-5554 shell svc data enable
```

The caller log should then show `the socket came back`, then `the request is already PICKED_UP` (or `EN_ROUTE_HOSPITAL`), then `leg 2 started`. The van should leave the pickup point and drive toward the hospital.

That reload uses `GET /api/v1/emergency-requests/:requestId`, which returns the same payload as the socket event, including the hospital. If the hospital drive is already running, a second pickup is ignored.

Verified from the code, not from the demo:
- The spinner is _EmergencySearchScreen in madad_plus_mobile/lib/emergency_flow.dart. The title is "Finding help". It shows a CircularProgressIndicator. While isRequesting is true the subtitle is "Looking for the nearest free ambulance." When isRequesting is false the subtitle is "Waiting to hear back from dispatch." The screen passes no onBack, so the frame has no back button.
- The only assignment of currentScreen = EmergencyScreen.emergencySearch is requestAmbulance() in madad_plus_mobile/lib/services/emergency_request_state.dart. On mobile that line is 1643. On mobiletest it is 1684.
- requestAmbulance sets isRequesting to true, switches to that screen, then awaits EmergencyService.createEmergencyRequest. That method POSTs to /api/v1/emergency-requests. EmergencyService._send applies requestTimeout, which is 45 seconds.
- If the result status is QUEUED, the screen becomes emergencyBusy. For every other status it becomes emergencyAssigned, then beginCallerLeg, _connectToRequest, and _startArrivalSimulation run. _connectToRequest is the first time the phone joins the request socket. A socket event cannot move the phone off the spinner before that POST returns.
- TimeoutException, ApiException, and any other error set the screen back to emergencyConfirm. The finally block sets isRequesting to false and calls notifyListeners.
- src/server.js inserts the row as QUEUED, then assignNearest in src/dispatch.js, then sends 201. The phone waits for that whole handler.
- The transcript has no log and no saved subtitle from the frozen demo. Do not invent which subtitle was on screen.

## Objective
Stop Register as Provider from creating a second provider when the typed business name matches an existing provider in the same trade. Exact matches are refused. Partial matches ask "Is this you?" and only the bottom button creates an account.

## Context
Checkout is mobiletest. Do not commit, push, or switch branches.

Register as Provider is `_RegisterScreen` in `madad_plus_mobile/lib/emergency_flow.dart`. Continue calls `registerProvider` in `madad_plus_mobile/lib/services/emergency_request_state.dart`, which posts to `POST /api/v1/providers` in `src/server.js` and then opens the dummy code screen. The route inserts a row when the phone and CNIC are free. It does not compare names, so "Raja circuitry and electrical works" and "raja circuitry and electrical works" both exist today. The capital-R row has already been deleted. Leave the remaining row, `raja circuitry and electrical works`, phone `0315 6767679`, in the database.

The provider list for a trade comes from `GET /api/v1/providers`. A match must be limited to the trade selected on the form. The trade chips are Carpenter, Plumber, and Electrician, stored through `specialisation_id`.

## Target state
On Continue, before any insert, compare the typed name with providers in the selected trade only.

Normalize both names by trimming, collapsing repeated spaces, and ignoring letter case.

Exact: the normalized names are equal. Do not insert. Stay on the register screen and show: "A user already exists with that name."

Partial, only when the names are not exact:
- One full normalized name contains the other.
- Or the Levenshtein distance between the two full normalized names is 1 or 2, and both names are at least 8 characters.
Do not match on a shared word by itself. "Raja plumbing" does not match "raja circuitry and electrical works".

If there is at least one partial match, open a page whose heading is "Is this you?". Show every match with its name, its full phone number, and its CNIC. Keep the first 5 digits of the CNIC and replace every later digit with x. Leave dashes and spaces in place, so `42201-8888888-1` is shown as `42201-xxxxxxx-x`. The server must return the CNIC already masked. Do not send the full CNIC in this response.

Tapping a result opens that provider's dashboard. No row is inserted.

A button at the bottom of that page reads "Create account". That button is the only action that inserts the typed name, phone, CNIC, and trade. After it succeeds, keep the existing dummy verification screen and then open the new provider's dashboard.

If there is no exact or partial match, keep today's path: insert, dummy code, dashboard.

## Scope
- Work only in `src/server.js`, `madad_plus_mobile/lib/emergency_flow.dart`, `madad_plus_mobile/lib/services/emergency_request_state.dart`, `madad_plus_mobile/lib/services/emergency_service.dart`, and `madad_plus_mobile/test/widget_test.dart`.
- Do not touch driver registration, caller registration, `.env`, `package-lock.json`, or the database schema.
- Do not delete the remaining raja provider.

## Constraints
- Match the style already in those files.
- No new dependency. Implement the distance check in the server file.
- The server must reject an exact match even if the app asks it to create the account.
- Only make the changes described here.

## Acceptance criteria
- Typing the same name as an existing provider in the same trade, with different capital letters, shows "A user already exists with that name." and adds no row.
- Typing "Raja circuitry" while "raja circuitry and electrical works" is an Electrician shows "Is this you?" with that provider, the phone, and the masked CNIC.
- A one-character or two-character typo in a name of at least 8 characters shows the same page.
- A shared word that is not contained as the full name, and is not a 1 or 2 character typo, does not match.
- A provider in a different trade does not match.
- Tapping a result opens that provider's dashboard and the provider count stays the same.
- "Create account" inserts the new provider and then shows the dummy code screen.
- `flutter test --plain-name "a new provider registers"` passes, along with new tests for the exact, partial, typo, and select-existing cases.

## Action boundaries
- Inspect and edit the files listed above.
- Stop before any database delete, schema change, commit, or push.

## Progress evidence
Report the new route behavior with the response status for an exact match, a partial match, and a create. Paste the passing test names.

For the dashboard tests that tap into job requests, I'm realizing they likely call openJob directly on the session state and then pump, relying on the existing Accept job screen rather than new logic. I also need to figure out whether flutter_local_notifications can be added to pubspec and whether the notification service should be made injectable so tests avoid hitting the real platform channel.

I'm designing a NotificationService class with requestPermission and showNewJobs methods plus an onTap callback, letting EmergencyRequestState accept an optional notification service so tests can pass a silent fake while production uses the real one. Since tests construct EmergencyRequestState without a notification service, the default real implementation would otherwise trigger a MissingPluginException in the widget test environment, so I need to wrap the real service's calls in try/catch to swallow platform channel failures when running under the test harness's simulated Android target.

I'm also realizing it might be cleaner to make the notifier nullable by default (no notifications unless supplied) and have main.dart inject the real service, which I should verify. Separately, I need to check the Android build.gradle for core library desugaring and compileSdk settings required by flutter_local_notifications, and I'm noticing the large icon setup is problematic since DrawableResourceAndroidBitmap looks up resources in the drawable folder, not mipmap, so ic_launcher won't resolve there and I'll likely need to copy the icon into a drawable resource folder under a different name.

For the small icon I'll create a simple white vector drawable, maybe a plus/cross symbol for the brand. I also need to handle the Android 13 runtime notification permission request through the platform-specific implementation, and wire up the tap handler for notification responses.

For the foreground case the callback opens incoming requests directly, while a killed app just opens the normal start screen per the plan, and I'll set the Android channel importance to high for heads-up banners. In the booking state update logic, I'm treating a booking as new when it isn't already in the list and its status is PENDING, since there's no explicit event name being passed through.

Since the plan doesn't explicitly address offline suppression, I'll stick to the literal rule: trigger the banner whenever a new pending job arrives while the provider isn't already on the incoming screen, regardless of their status, and leave the incoming count behavior as-is since the plan doesn't say otherwise. For the cancel flow, I'm looking at the accept route's style to model a new PATCH endpoint for cancellation, and I need to update the caller-side cancel logic so it actually calls the cancellation service when there's an active domestic booking, while treating server errors from already-accepted requests as safe to ignore.

cancelDomestic is shared by both the pre-booking cancel path and the post-booking "Cancel request" path, so I'll only fire the server cancel call when there's an existing domestic booking still in PENDING status -- this naturally skips the case where cancelAssignedProvider calls it after acceptance, since the booking would already be ACCEPTED by then, and the server itself rejects non-PENDING cancellations as a backstop. The reply recorded:

The log shows `crash_dump64: failed to attach to thread` and "Lost connection to device", this points to an actual native crash, not just a missing timeout. The crash happens around the time the user presses Find my location, but without the Java stack trace I can't pinpoint exactly where.

The plan should start with capturing `adb logcat` output right after the tap to get the ANR trace or tombstone. Worth considering: this emulator is `gphone16k` (16 KB page size, Android 16), which has known issues with native libraries that aren't 16KB-aligned, that could be the root cause if a library like geolocator or Impeller isn't compatible. It's also possible the crash_dump lines are actually ANR stack dumps (debuggerd gets invoked for those too), which would mean the main thread is genuinely blocked, possibly inside the Flutter geolocator call waiting on a location fix that never arrives on the emulator.

Rather than asking the user, I'll flag minor decisions and just pick reasonable defaults, like a 15-second timeout for the location call (keeping it shorter than the existing 20-second reverse-geocode timeout) and noting that the other two callers of `locateDevice` will inherit the same limit, which seems acceptable. For testability without mocking Geolocator directly, I'm considering adding an optional constructor parameter for reading position so tests can inject their own behavior, though I still need to account for the service-enabled and permission checks Geolocator also performs.

Another approach: override `GeolocatorPlatform.instance` with a fake implementation via the platform interface package, which should be feasible since it supports mocking through MockPlatformInterfaceMixin even as a transitive dependency.

For timeout testing, I can simulate the delay with fakeAsync or by pumping widgets forward in time. The network call in labelForCoordinates will naturally fail in the test environment since HTTP is blocked, falling back to the 'Current location' label -- which actually simplifies the test setup since no network mocking is needed.

As for the ANR cause itself, I shouldn't guess at a fix without diagnosing it from logcat first -- if the main-thread block traces to something unrelated like geolocator service binding or an emulator-specific issue, I need to stop and report that rather than assume.

I'm also thinking about `_saveDevice`, which currently relies on `saveHomePlace` that mutates homeAddress -- I need a separate `addSavedPlace` method that only appends to the homePlaces list without touching homeAddress or the chosen-key field, and ideally factor out the shared persistence logic to avoid duplicating the write path.

I'll go with extraction to avoid duplicating the JSON encoding logic. Checking existing tests, I see nothing conflicts, "Find my location" references a different screen, so this change should be isolated. I also want to confirm that when the saved list is empty, adding a found place correctly surfaces it with visible on-screen feedback.

The row simply appearing at the top likely serves as sufficient feedback without needing an extra confirmation control, since nothing in the spec asks for one. The existing tap behavior on the row (selecting the home place and navigating home) and the duplicate-address handling (removing and re-inserting at top) both already work as expected, so I'm ready to write up the plan concisely with todos, without adding further questions.

## Context
Madad+ Flutter app at madad_plus_mobile, backend at src/server.js. Payment review is _CostReviewScreen in madad_plus_mobile/lib/emergency_flow.dart. Money decisions live in EmergencyRequestState.submitRepairTotal and decideRepairTotal in madad_plus_mobile/lib/services/emergency_request_state.dart. The booking payload is DomesticBooking in madad_plus_mobile/lib/services/emergency_service.dart and domesticRequestPayload in src/server.js.

Today the provider types up to 3 component rows locally, then submitRepairTotal sends only quotedTotal. The customer review then shows "Repair total", "Inspection fee", and "Total", with Accept and Refuse. Accept calls decideRepairTotal(accept: true), which charges inspection fee plus quoted total and opens the existing rating screen (DomesticJob.complete). The user asked:

how do i apply the new miggration and restart the server?

Skills attached with this message: i-have-adhd

The reply recorded:

Paste this SQL into the Render database shell. The app calls `https://madadplus.onrender.com`, and this folder has no migrate command.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS receipt_components (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name varchar(150) NOT NULL,
  price decimal(12, 2) NOT NULL,
  position integer NOT NULL,
  receipt_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES receipts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS receipt_components_receipt_id_index
  ON receipt_components (receipt_id);
```

1. Open the Render Postgres database for Madad+ and run that SQL. About 2 minutes.
2. On the Render web service, click Manual Deploy so the new server code starts. About 3 minutes.

A local `npm start` only restarts a server on your machine. The phones keep using Render until that deploy finishes.

Next: run the SQL, then tell me the first error line if Render rejects it.

[madad+ demo v5.5](931f1154-c71a-4b9d-8c39-a8d87a289f41) stopped on the pitch, after three turns. The code was not touched.

You asked why Madad+ is unique. The answer was one Karachi app that assigns the nearest free ambulance and shows the closer unit it skipped, and that books a plumber, electrician, or carpenter only after the customer accepts a line-by-line bill.

You said a person does not need both services at once. The answer was that they open the app for one job, and the saved address is already there the next time the other job happens.

You said two apps can both store an address and a phone number. The answer was that a saved address is just login. The reason to pick Madad+ is the decision on the job in front of them:

1. Ambulance: the app picks the nearest free unit, shows the closer one it skipped, keeps the same request through pickup, hospital, and drop-off, and can reassign it if that driver becomes unavailable.
2. Repair: the app stores each part, checks that those prices add up to the quoted total, shows the inspection fee on its own line, and waits for accept or refuse.

The user asked:

can you explain how the syncing of ambulance driver and user is working here in a non technical way?

Skills attached with this message: i-have-adhd

The reply recorded:

Each phone draws its own ambulance and slides it along the road. How far it has moved depends on how long the trip has been going.

The server remembers the moment the ambulance was assigned. The caller's phone and the driver's phone both use that same moment. If the driver signs out and signs back in, their phone reads that saved moment and the ambulance picture jumps to where the caller's picture already is.

The dispatcher page is separate. When you mark an ambulance unavailable there, the server tells that driver's phone, and the badge on the phone changes to match.

Your last command left out the phone id after `-d`, so Flutter treated the Gemini line as a device name. The key in that command is now in this chat. Make a new one in Google AI Studio, then run:

```bat
flutter run --profile -d 1643825625006053 --dart-define=GEMINI_API_KEY=YOUR_NEW_KEY
```

The user asked:

that doesnt explain how syncing works, like how do i explain how the icon on the driver portal and the icon on the user portal is moving at almost the same pace?

The reply recorded:

Neither phone sends its ambulance position to the other. Both phones calculate the position separately, from the same three facts, so they land on the same spot.

1. **Same start time.** The server stores the moment the ambulance was assigned, and both phones read it.
2. **Same trip.** Both phones get the same start point (the ambulance) and the same end point (the caller).
3. **Same speed.** Both use the same rule: the trip lasts the road distance divided by 55 km/h, kept between 8 and 45 seconds.

Each phone then asks "how much of the trip time has passed since the start time?" and puts the icon that far along the road. Same start time and same trip length give the same answer on both screens, so the icons move together without talking to each other.

It is a demo simulation. The icon is not following real GPS.

You can say this to the panel: "Both phones use the same start time and the same speed, so each one works out where the ambulance should be. They agree because the maths is the same, not because they send each other positions."

The user asked:

and how is the distance to the nearest ambulance from a user's location being found?

Skills attached with this message: i-have-adhd

The reply recorded:

The server finds the nearest ambulance by straight-line distance, as a bird flies, not by road.

1. **Caller location.** The caller's phone sends its map pin position with the request. The server saves it as the pickup point.
2. **Ambulance locations.** Every ambulance has a saved location in the database.
3. **Who counts.** Only ambulances marked FREE are considered. Busy and unavailable ones are skipped, and so is any ambulance already blocked for that request.
4. **Ranking.** The database (PostGIS, the map add-on for the database) sorts those free ambulances from closest to farthest from the pickup point.
5. **Assigning.** The server gives the request to the closest one. If that one is taken at the same moment, it tries the next closest.
6. **Nobody free.** The request waits in a queue until an ambulance becomes free.

The server also looks at the closest ambulance of any status, in kilometres. If that one is busy, the app shows it as "considered nearest", so you can say the closest one was busy and the next one was sent.

Because the distance is a straight line, the nearest ambulance on the map may not be the fastest by road. The panel might ask about that.

Next: if you want the exact lines, open `src/dispatch.js` and search for `assignNearest`.

I'm tracing how dispatch picks the nearest free ambulance using PostGIS's straight-line distance operator, ordering candidates by proximity and trying each in sequence, while a separate "consideredNearest" calculation also uses straight-line distance to find the closest ambulance regardless of availability.

## What to apply
Two published fixes for a Leaflet picture that disappears while the marker stays. Apply both. They are small and they do not fight each other.

1. Own the image the way Leaflet owns an image marker. A divIcon img is destroyed every time setIcon runs, and the new img can fail to paint. Build one L.icon per status with iconUrl, iconSize, and iconAnchor, and reuse that object. On a status change, point the existing marker at the cached icon for the new status. Do not build a new HTML string on a timer, a socket event, or a poll. Sources: the failed A-07 run, where the tooltip survived and the picture did not, and Leaflet divIcon image threads such as https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55133973/leaflet-divicon-not-displaying-on-map-in-angular.

2. Keep the marker pane composited during pan and zoom. Add will-change: transform on .leaflet-marker-pane in style.css. Leaflet issues https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet/issues/8068 and https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet/issues/8933 document markers and controls that vanish during movement, with will-change: transform and transform: translate3d(0,0,0) as the fixes that held. Do not add top or left on .ambulance-marker. Those rules override iconAnchor: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54328065/custom-leaflet-divicon-not-staying-in-fixed-marker-position-when-zoomed.

Google's own marker docs require an anchor so the icon stays on its lat/lng when the zoom changes, and scaledSize for the drawn size: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/markers. The scale people use so a vehicle covers the same ground as you zoom is pixelSizeAtZoom0 * 2^zoom, capped so the bitmap does not grow without limit: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/3281524/resize-markers-depending-on-zoom-google-maps-v3.

On this map, do that in Leaflet. On the map zoom event, set the ambulance pixel size to round(referenceSize * 2^(zoom - referenceZoom)), with the anchor at the center (size / 2, size / 2). referenceSize is 41. referenceZoom is the zoom where the van matches the closer crop above, beside the hospital pin, about one plot wide. Measure that zoom in the browser. Do not invent it. Cap the size at 41 so street-level zoom does not grow the van past the closer crop. Set a floor around 12 so a city-wide view still shows a dot on the exact point. Resize without requesting ambulance.png again. Hospital icons stay 40 by 40.

## Objective
Keep every ambulance picture painted on the dispatcher map for the whole call. A status change, a position update, the 15-second sync, and the drive animation must leave the van visible. The tooltip staying up while the van is blank is the failure.

## Context
The dispatcher is http://localhost:5500. The page is madadplus-web/index.html. The map code is madadplus-web/app.js. Styles are madadplus-web/style.css. The map is Leaflet.

The van is already an L.icon, cached in ambulanceIcons and built in ambulanceIcon() around line 194. resizeAmbulanceMarkers() changes width, height, and margin on the existing img and does not call setIcon. upsertAmbulanceMarker() still calls setIcon when ambulanceMarkers[id].options.icon !== icon. That runs on every status change because the cache key is "STATUS:size".

This same blank-van bug was fixed once by leaving the divIcon path. It came back. Do not treat the current setIcon guard as the finished fix. Read the current functions before editing.

Zoom size stays as it is: 41px at zoom 16, half that for each zoom level out, never under 12px, never over 41px. A-07 beside Niazi Hospital at zoom 16 is the size check.

## Two fixes to choose from
These are the two durable fixes from Leaflet issue 561 (https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet/issues/561) and the setIcon DOM reuse in Leaflet PR 1726 (https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet/pull/1726). Read both before editing. Use one. Say which one and why in the reply.

1. Stop calling setIcon after the marker exists. Change the picture by setting the existing img src: marker.getElement().src = newUrl. Leaflet maintainers recorded this on issue 561 because setIcon destroys or rewrites the icon DOM while the marker is live.
2. Draw the van as a DivIcon whose picture is a CSS background-image, not an img src. The Leaflet maintainer recommended that on the same issue when the icon has to change while the marker is on the map. ## Objective
A new ambulance call searches outward in rings. The dispatcher map draws that ring. One free ambulance inside the ring is assigned as today. More than one free ambulance inside the ring gets the booking on the driver phone, and the first driver to tap Accept is assigned. The others lose it.

## Distances
Start at 300 m. Each ring lasts 15 seconds. If no free ambulance is inside at the end of the ring, grow by 500 m and repeat: 300, then 800, then 1300, and so on. Distance is straight-line metres, the same measure src/dispatch.js uses now. Only FREE ambulances count. Busy and unavailable ones are skipped, and so is any ambulance already blocked for that request.

Count at the end of the 15 seconds, so a second ambulance can enter during the ring.
- 0 free: start the next ring.
- 1 free: assign that ambulance the way assignNearest assigns one today. Stop the ring.
- 2 or more free: send the booking to those drivers. Stop the ring. The first Accept is assigned. Decline, or no tap before the next 15 seconds, starts the next ring from the radius just reached.

If the organisation has no FREE ambulance at all, use the queue that already exists. Do not grow the ring forever.

## Dispatcher circle
This file is on Webtest: madadplus-web/app.js, with styles in madadplus-web/style.css. It is not on mobiletest. Do not create madadplus-web on mobiletest. Do not checkout another branch. The ring is drawn around the call's pickup point. It grows smoothly across the 15 seconds, from the radius already on screen to the next radius. It starts from the value on screen, so a new ring does not jump. When a driver is assigned, the ring stops where it is. With reduced motion, the ring appears at the end radius of that step instead of moving.

## Server
On mobiletest, change src/dispatch.js. assignNearest currently orders every FREE ambulance by straight-line distance and assigns the closest. Replace that search with the rings above. One ambulance still goes through assignSpecific. Several ambulances are offered, not assigned, until one driver accepts.

Two actions: Decline and Accept. Accept assigns that driver if nobody else has taken it. If somebody else already took it, say the call was taken. Pressing a button responds on the press. Do not add a fare, a car name, a rating, or a photo. Those are on the InDrive reference and this call does not have them.

A driver who was not offered sees the same screen they see today.

1. Paste this after the `socket.on("request.completed", ...)` handler:

```js
// ---- Search ring (search.updated / search.ended from the server) ----
// One circle per request, centred on its dispatch point. Each update grows
// it from the radius already drawn to the next ring across 15 seconds.
// search.ended stops it where it is.
const searchRings = {}; // request id -> { circle, frame }
const reducedMotion = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)");

function stopSearchRing(requestId) {
  const ring = searchRings[requestId];
  if (ring) cancelAnimationFrame(ring.frame);
}

function removeSearchRing(requestId) {
  const ring = searchRings[requestId];
  if (!ring) return;
  cancelAnimationFrame(ring.frame);
  map.removeLayer(ring.circle);
  delete searchRings[requestId];
}

function drawSearchRing(payload) {
  if (!map || !payload || !payload.requestId || !payload.center) return;
  const center = [payload.center.lat, payload.center.lng];
  let ring = searchRings[payload.requestId];
  if (!ring) {
    const color = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--accent-critical").trim();
    ring = {
      circle: L.circle(center, {
        radius: payload.fromRadius || 0,
        color,
        weight: 2,
        fillColor: color,
        fillOpacity: 0.08,
        interactive: false
      }).addTo(map),
      frame: null
    };
    searchRings[payload.requestId] = ring;
  }
  stopSearchRing(payload.requestId);
  ring.circle.setLatLng(center);

const from = ring.circle.getRadius();
  const to = payload.toRadius;
  if (reducedMotion.matches || !payload.durationMs || from === to) {
    ring.circle.setRadius(to);
    return;
  }
  const start = performance.now();
  function step(now) {
    const t = Math.min(1, (now - start) / payload.durationMs);
    ring.circle.setRadius(from + (to - from) * t);
    if (t < 1) ring.frame = requestAnimationFrame(step);
  }
  ring.frame = requestAnimationFrame(step);
}

socket.on("search.updated", drawSearchRing);
socket.on("search.ended", (payload) => {
  if (payload && payload.requestId) stopSearchRing(payload.requestId);
});
```

## What to apply
Two published fixes for a Leaflet picture that disappears while the marker stays. Apply both. They are small and they do not fight each other.

1. Own the image the way Leaflet owns an image marker. A divIcon img is destroyed every time setIcon runs, and the new img can fail to paint. Build one L.icon per status with iconUrl, iconSize, and iconAnchor, and reuse that object. On a status change, point the existing marker at the cached icon for the new status. Do not build a new HTML string on a timer, a socket event, or a poll. Sources: the failed A-07 run, where the tooltip survived and the picture did not, and Leaflet divIcon image threads such as https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55133973/leaflet-divicon-not-displaying-on-map-in-angular.

2. Keep the marker pane composited during pan and zoom. Add will-change: transform on .leaflet-marker-pane in style.css. Leaflet issues https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet/issues/8068 and https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet/issues/8933 document markers and controls that vanish during movement, with will-change: transform and transform: translate3d(0,0,0) as the fixes that held. Do not add top or left on .ambulance-marker. Those rules override iconAnchor: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54328065/custom-leaflet-divicon-not-staying-in-fixed-marker-position-when-zoomed.

Google's own marker docs require an anchor so the icon stays on its lat/lng when the zoom changes, and scaledSize for the drawn size: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/markers. The scale people use so a vehicle covers the same ground as you zoom is pixelSizeAtZoom0 * 2^zoom, capped so the bitmap does not grow without limit: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/3281524/resize-markers-depending-on-zoom-google-maps-v3.

On this map, do that in Leaflet. On the map zoom event, set the ambulance pixel size to round(referenceSize * 2^(zoom - referenceZoom)), with the anchor at the center (size / 2, size / 2). referenceSize is 41. referenceZoom is the zoom where the van matches the closer crop above, beside the hospital pin, about one plot wide. Measure that zoom in the browser. Do not invent it. Cap the size at 41 so street-level zoom does not grow the van past the closer crop. Set a floor around 12 so a city-wide view still shows a dot on the exact point. Resize without requesting ambulance.png again. Hospital icons stay 40 by 40.
